129402.q: A buyer sends you a screenshot of a payment and wants the goods straight away. Nothing has arrived in your account. What do you do?
a: Wait until the money is credited to your account
Transfer money back to the buyer
129402.e: Screenshots are easy to fake. Only the credit in your account counts.

129403.q: In Switzerland, how long is a seller legally liable for defects in new goods if the contract says nothing else?
129403.e: The statutory warranty is 2 years. But it can be limited or excluded in the contract, so it is worth looking at the terms.
129403.m: 2 years by law, but read the contract.

129404.q: Why is a guarantee by private individuals in Switzerland bound by strict formal rules?
a: To protect guarantors from rash promises with serious consequences
So they can be agreed more quickly
129404.e: A guarantor can lose a lot of money. That is why the law requires, for example, written form and, for larger amounts, a notarised deed.

129405.q: What does a bank take on with an asset management mandate?
a: It decides on the investments itself within the agreed limits
It only runs a savings account
129405.e: The customer sets the strategy and risk, then the bank buys and sells by itself. It charges a fee for this.
129405.m: With a mandate, the bank decides on your behalf.

129406.q: What must a financial services provider check before giving investment advice?
a: Whether the investment suits the customer’s knowledge, goals and finances
How many brothers and sisters the customer has
Only the age of the parents
129406.e: Under the Financial Services Act, they must check whether a product suits the customer. This protects against investments that are too risky.
129406.m: The investment must suit the customer.

129407.q: What is a key information document for a financial product for?
a: It briefly sums up the risks, costs and how it works
129407.e: The document is meant to make different products comparable. You should read it before buying.
129407.m: Read the key information document before buying.

129408.q: What does a share index such as the SPI show?
a: The performance of many shares summed up in one number
The price of a single share
129408.e: An index bundles the prices of many companies. The SPI covers a large part of the shares traded on the Swiss stock exchange.
129408.m: An index sums up many prices.

129409.q: Elias works for a company and invests all his savings in its shares. Which risk is especially big?
a: Concentration risk: his pay and savings depend on the same company
The risk of getting too much interest
A currency risk with the euro
129409.e: If the company does badly, he may lose his job and his savings at the same time. Spreading widely reduces this risk.
129409.m: Do not put all your eggs in one basket.

129410.q: If you invest in dollars but think in francs, what extra risk do you carry?
a: An interest risk on your savings account
129410.e: If the dollar falls against the franc, the value of the investment in francs drops, even if the share stays the same.

129411.q: A provider promises a 2% return per month, guaranteed and risk-free. Roughly how much would that be per year without compound interest?
a: Exactly the same as a savings account
129411.e: 12 months times 2% makes 24% a year. A guarantee like this with no risk is a clear warning sign of fraud.
129411.m: Convert monthly returns into yearly ones.

129412.q: How many 20-centime coins make 2 francs altogether?
129412.e: 2 francs are 200 centimes. 200 divided by 20 makes 10 coins.

129413.q: Lio has 1 franc. He buys chewing gum for 40 centimes. How much does he have left?
129413.e: 1 franc is 100 centimes. 100 minus 40 makes 60 centimes.
129413.m: For sums, one franc has 100 centimes.

129414.q: Every day Nora puts 50 centimes in her money box. How much does she have after 6 days?
129414.e: 6 times 50 centimes makes 300 centimes. That is 3 francs.
129414.m: Even small coins add up to a lot.

129415.e: 100 centimes are 1 franc. So 300 centimes are 3 francs.

129416.e: 2 francs are 200 centimes, plus 50 centimes makes 250 centimes.

129417.q: A comic costs 6 francs, an exercise book 2 francs. How much more expensive is the comic?
129417.e: 6 minus 2 makes 4. The comic costs 4 francs more.
129417.m: You find the difference by subtracting.

129418.q: A toy car costs 8 francs. You have a 5-franc coin and two 2-franc coins. What is true?
a: It is enough and 1 franc is left over
129418.e: 5 plus 2 plus 2 makes 9 francs. After buying it, 1 franc is left.

129419.q: At the flea market Eva sells 3 books for 2 francs each. How much money does she get?

129420.q: A bread roll costs 80 centimes. How much do 2 bread rolls cost?
129420.e: 80 plus 80 centimes makes 160 centimes. That is 1 franc 60.

129421.q: Moritz wants a jigsaw puzzle for 15 francs. His grandfather gives him 10 francs towards it. How much does Moritz have to pay himself?
129421.e: 15 minus 10 makes 5. Moritz still pays 5 francs himself.
129421.m: A contribution makes the rest smaller.

129422.q: At the till you are given too much change by mistake. What do you do?
a: Say so and give the money back
129422.e: Otherwise the extra money will be missing from the till. Being honest is right.
129422.m: Too much change is given back.

129423.q: A friend wants to swap his game for your expensive bike. What do you do first?
a: Talk to your parents about it
129423.e: With valuable things, a swap is a big decision. Your parents help you see whether it is fair.
129423.m: Only swap valuable things with your parents’ help.

129424.q: Why are Swiss coins different sizes?
a: So you can tell them apart more easily
129424.e: Different sizes help you recognise the coins quickly, even without looking closely.
129424.m: The size helps you recognise them.

129425.q: Paula has 2 francs. She wants 5 pieces of chewing gum at 50 centimes each. What is true?
129425.e: 5 times 50 centimes is 2 francs 50. Paula only has 2 francs, so she is 50 centimes short.
129425.m: Work out beforehand whether it is enough.

129426.q: You want an ice cream for 2 francs and a drink for 3 francs, but you only have 4 francs. What do you do?
a: Run up a debt in the shop
129426.e: Together they cost 5 francs. With 4 francs you have to choose.
129426.m: If the money is not enough, you have to choose.

129427.q: What does the cashier in a shop do?
a: She adds up the prices and takes the money
129427.e: At the till, the goods are scanned, the prices added up and paid.
129427.m: The bill is settled at the till.

129428.q: Granny gives you 20 francs for a week’s holiday. What is smart?
a: Spend only part of it each day
Spend it all on the first day
129428.e: If you divide the money up, you still have some on the last day of the holiday.
129428.m: Divide up your holiday money well.

a: Money a class collects together for trips
The till in the grocery shop
The teacher’s account for her pay
129429.e: The class fund contains money that belongs to everyone, for example from a cake sale.
129429.m: The class fund belongs to everyone.

129430.q: Why is nobody allowed to simply take money from the class fund?
a: Because the money belongs to everyone together
129430.e: Shared money is only used for what everyone has agreed.

129431.q: You want to count a big jar full of coins. What is the easiest way?
a: First sort the coins by type
129431.e: Once the coins are sorted, you count each type and then add them up.

129432.q: Why is it practical to always get your pocket money on the same day?
a: You can plan better how long it has to last
Because otherwise you may not spend it
129432.e: If you know when the next pocket money is coming, you can divide it up well.
129432.m: A fixed day helps with planning.

129433.q: Lotta wants earrings for 9 francs. She has 3 francs and saves another 2 francs every week. How many weeks does she need?
129433.e: She is 6 francs short. At 2 francs a week, that takes 3 weeks.
129433.m: First work out what is missing.

129434.q: A book costs 7 francs. A game costs twice as much. How much does the game cost?
129434.e: Twice means times 2. 7 times 2 makes 14 francs.
129434.m: Twice as much means times two.

129435.q: Ena has 5 francs. Her friend has 3 francs more than her. How much does the friend have?
129435.e: 3 francs more than 5 francs is 8 francs.

129436.q: What helps you remember your savings goal?
a: Sticking a picture of it on your money box
Hiding the money box and forgetting it
129436.e: If you can see your goal, you are less likely to spend the money on something else.
129436.m: A visible goal helps you save.

129437.q: Leo and Mia each want a tub of ice cream for 4 francs. Together they have 10 francs. How much is left over?
129437.e: Two tubs cost 8 francs. 10 minus 8 makes 2 francs.

129438.q: What helps visually impaired people tell Swiss banknotes apart?
129438.e: Swiss notes are different lengths and have tactile markings. So you can also tell them apart by touch.

129439.q: A shop takes back a jumper even though it does not have to. What is this called?
129439.e: Goodwill is a voluntary gesture. You have no right to it.

129440.q: Why is it not a good idea to pay for a holiday with a loan?
a: The holiday is over, but the debt and interest remain
Because the bank then comes along
129440.e: You keep paying long after the holiday, plus interest. It is better to save beforehand.

129441.q: In online banking you enter a payment today with an execution date of the 25th. What happens?
a: The payment is only made on the 25th
It is repeated every month on the 25th
129441.e: With an execution date you plan a single payment in advance. A standing order, by contrast, would repeat.

129442.q: Lea gets 80 francs youth allowance a month. She spends 35 francs on clothes and 20 francs on going out. How much is left?
129442.e: 35 plus 20 makes 55 francs. 80 minus 55 makes 25 francs.
129442.m: What is left can be saved.

129443.q: Someone shares a link in the group chat: “Free 50 francs credit for everyone, just log in quickly!” What do you do?
a: Not click and warn the group
Post your password in the chat
129443.e: Links like this often lead to fake sites that steal login details.
129443.m: Free money links are usually traps.

129444.q: What is one risk of saving your card details in many online shops?
a: They can be stolen in a data leak
You can no longer pay in cash
129444.e: The more shops have the details, the greater the danger that they fall into the wrong hands in an attack.

129445.q: In this example 1 euro costs 90 centimes. How many francs do 10 euros cost?
129445.e: 10 times 90 centimes makes 900 centimes, so 9 francs.
129445.m: Amount times rate gives the price in francs.

129446.q: Some banks charge a fee for paper bank statements. How can you save it?
a: View the statements digitally in the app or online banking
129446.e: Digital statements are often free and can be viewed at any time.

129447.q: After your holiday you still have some euro coins. What is often true?
a: Many banks only exchange notes, not coins
You get coins back twice over
Euro coins also count as francs in Switzerland
You have to throw them away
129447.e: Foreign coins are usually not exchanged. It is better to use them on your next holiday or donate them.
129447.m: Spend foreign coins before going home.

129448.q: What does the date with month and year on the front of a bank card show?
a: Until when the card is valid
129448.e: After this date the card no longer works. The bank usually sends a new one beforehand.

129449.q: You have received a new bank card. What do you do with the old one?
a: Cut it through the chip and dispose of it
129449.e: The old card still has data on it. Once cut up, nobody can misuse it.

129450.q: Why should you never read your card number out loud on the phone on a train?
a: Other people can listen in and misuse it
Because the number then becomes invalid
129450.e: Card details are like a key. Anyone listening could shop online with them.
129450.m: Never say card details out loud.

129451.q: A classmate keeps borrowing money from you and never pays it back. What is sensible?
a: Talk about it openly and lend him nothing more
Tell everyone in the chat about it
129451.e: Someone who pays nothing back is abusing your trust. An open conversation and clear limits help.

129452.q: When hiring a bike you pay a 50-franc deposit. What happens to it?
a: You get it back if the bike comes back undamaged
It then belongs to the owner for ever
It is transferred to your savings account
129452.e: A deposit is security for the owner. If you bring the bike back undamaged, you get the money back.

129453.q: Why do many banks offer young people free accounts?
a: They hope to keep them as customers later
Because young people are not allowed money
Because the National Bank pays for it
129453.e: People who open an account when young often stay with the same bank for a long time. That is why it pays off for the banks.
129453.m: Free accounts are meant to win customers.

129454.q: How often do apprentices usually receive their wage?
a: Only at the end of the apprenticeship
129454.e: As with most employees, the apprentice wage is transferred to the account every month.

129455.q: What is the difference between saving in an account and investing, for example in shares?
a: Investing offers more chances but also risks of loss
129455.e: Money in an account is safe but earns little. With investments the value can rise or fall.

129456.q: When you pay at the post office counter, which part of a QR bill stays with you as proof?
129456.e: The QR bill has a payment part and a receipt. You keep the receipt as proof.

129457.q: Jana wants to have 150 francs for a concert in 5 months. How much does she have to save each month?
129457.e: 150 francs divided by 5 months makes 30 francs a month.
129457.m: Goal divided by time gives the monthly amount.

129458.q: You see in the app that a purchase has been charged twice. What do you do?
a: Keep the receipt and contact the shop or bank
Give the shop a bad review and forget it
129458.e: Double charges happen. With the receipt the mistake can be corrected.

a: Many people fund a project together with small amounts
A bank lends one person a lot of money
129459.e: Through internet platforms, many people support, for example, a book, a game or an idea.

129460.q: In Switzerland, how can you recognise charities that handle donations carefully?
a: By the ZEWO seal of approval
By a Swiss cross in the logo
By a phone number starting with 0800
129460.e: The ZEWO foundation checks non-profit organisations. Its seal shows that donations are used for their intended purpose.
129460.m: The ZEWO seal stands for checked charities.

129461.q: Tim has an overdraft with high interest and an interest-free loan from his parents. Which is it sensible to pay back first?
a: The debt with the highest interest
Always the smaller debt, whatever the interest
129461.e: Expensive debts cost the most every month. If you pay them off first, you save interest.
129461.m: Pay off the most expensive debts first.

129462.q: Market interest rates rise sharply. What usually happens to the price of bonds already issued with low interest?
129462.e: New bonds then pay more interest. Old ones with low interest are less in demand and lose value.
129462.m: Interest rates up, bond prices down.

129463.q: What does a bond’s rating tell you?
a: How creditworthy the borrower is judged to be
How popular the company is with customers
129463.e: Rating agencies assess how likely a borrower is to repay. A worse rating usually means higher interest and more risk.

129464.q: What distinguishes an actively managed fund from a passive index fund?
a: In an active fund, experts try to beat the market
The passive fund always has higher fees
The active fund only tracks an index
129464.e: Active funds pick securities deliberately and usually cost more. Passive funds simply track an index.

129465.q: When buying a home, at least 10% of the value must come from “hard” equity. What does not count?
129465.e: Pension fund money may be used, but it does not count as hard equity. That part has to be raised in other ways.
129465.m: Pension fund money is not hard equity.

129466.q: How does higher inflation affect the real value of existing debts with fixed interest?
a: It always stays exactly the same
129466.e: When prices and wages rise, the fixed debt amount is worth less in real terms. For savers, however, inflation is a disadvantage.
129466.m: Inflation weakens the real value of debts.

129467.q: In this example the rate is 1 euro = 0.95 francs. How many francs do 200 euros cost?

129468.q: What is the net return on an investment?
a: The return after deducting costs and taxes
The purchase price of the investment
129468.e: Fees and taxes reduce the return. What counts is what is actually left at the end.

129469.q: Luca earns 4000 francs net and saves 400 francs of it a month. What is his savings rate?
129469.e: 400 out of 4000 is a tenth, so 10%.
129469.m: Savings rate = amount saved divided by income.

129470.q: A bike costs 500 francs. Prices rise by 4%. How much does it cost afterwards?
129470.e: 4% of 500 francs is 20 francs. 500 plus 20 makes 520 francs.
129470.m: Work out the percentage and add it on.

129471.q: Nicole’s pay rises by 1%, prices rise by 3%. What happens to her purchasing power?
129471.e: Prices rise more than her pay. So in real terms Nicole can afford less.
129471.m: A pay rise below inflation means less purchasing power.

129472.q: Up to what amount of interest per year is interest on a Swiss bank account exempt from withholding tax?
129472.e: If the interest on a customer’s balance is no more than 200 francs a year, no withholding tax is deducted.
129472.m: Up to 200 francs of interest, no withholding tax.

129473.q: How do people in Switzerland get back the withholding tax that was deducted?
a: By declaring their accounts and securities in their tax return
By applying to the National Bank
129473.e: If you declare your income correctly, you get the withholding tax back. It is meant to encourage honest tax returns.
129473.m: Declaring pays: you get the withholding tax back.

129474.q: What does it mean if a fund is “accumulating”?
a: Income is reinvested instead of paid out
Income is paid out in cash every month
129474.e: With accumulating funds, interest and dividends flow back into the fund. This strengthens the compound interest effect.

129475.q: What is an issue surcharge on an investment fund?
a: A one-off fee when buying fund units
129475.e: With the surcharge you pay more than the actual value of the unit when buying. This reduces the return.

129476.q: What is the spread when trading securities or currencies?
a: The difference between the buying and selling price
129476.e: If you buy and sell again immediately, you lose the spread. For rarely traded securities it is often large.
129476.m: The spread is a hidden fee.

129477.q: How do you calculate the market capitalisation of a listed company?
a: Share price times number of shares issued
129477.e: Market capitalisation shows how much all the shares together are worth on the stock exchange.
129477.m: Price times number of shares gives the market value.

129478.q: What is a stock market flotation, also called an IPO?
a: A company offers its shares publicly on the stock exchange for the first time
A walk to the stock exchange
The closing of a stock exchange
129478.e: With a flotation a company raises capital. After that anyone can buy its shares.
129478.m: IPO: on the stock exchange for the first time.

129479.q: What do you normally get back at the end of a bond’s term if the borrower can pay?
129479.e: During the term there is interest, and at the end the nominal value is repaid.
129479.m: At the end you get the nominal value back.

129480.q: What does the coupon of a bond refer to?
129480.e: The coupon is the agreed interest that the borrower usually pays every year.

129481.q: Why do bonds of the Swiss Confederation usually pay less interest than bonds of small companies?
a: The Confederation is seen as a very safe borrower
Companies are not allowed to pay interest
129481.e: Anyone who carries more risk demands more interest. With the Confederation the risk of default is very low.

129482.q: What is one disadvantage of gold as an investment?
a: It pays neither interest nor dividends
129482.e: Gold can only make a profit through a rising price. The price can also swing a lot.

129483.q: What does leverage do in a financial product?
129483.e: With leverage you move more money than you put in. Even small price movements can lead to big losses.

129484.q: A website is called almost the same as your bank, but with two letters swapped. What is this probably?
a: A fake site that wants to steal data
A site of the National Bank
129484.e: Fraudsters register addresses with small mistakes so that people mix them up. So check the address carefully or use the official app.
129484.m: One wrong letter can mean fraud.

129485.q: With artificial intelligence, voices can be imitated deceptively well. What helps families against fake emergency calls?
129485.e: If you ask for the code word, you quickly notice whether it really is a family member calling.
129485.m: A code word exposes fake calls.

129486.q: What characterises a loan with annuity repayments?
a: Equal instalments made up of interest and repayment
You only pay interest, never the money back
You pay everything on the first day
129486.e: With annuities the instalment stays the same. The interest part falls, the repayment part rises.

129487.q: For a loan with equal instalments, when is the interest part of the instalment largest?
a: At the start of the term
At the end of the term
129487.e: At the start the remaining debt is highest, so that is when the most interest is due.
129487.m: At the start you mainly pay interest.

129488.q: Sara earns 1000 francs net. She pays 200 board money at home, 40 for her phone, 70 for public transport and 150 for leisure. How much is left?
129488.e: 200 plus 40 plus 70 plus 150 makes 460 francs. 1000 minus 460 makes 540 francs.
129488.m: Add up all items, then subtract.

129489.q: How does a large part of the money in bank accounts come into being?
a: Through loans granted by commercial banks
129489.e: When a bank grants a loan, it credits the amount to an account. This creates new deposit money.
129489.m: Banks create deposit money through loans.

129490.q: What is meant by deposit money?
a: Balances in bank accounts that can be transferred
129490.e: Deposit money only exists as an entry at the bank. Today most payments are made with it.
129490.m: Deposit money is money in an account.

129491.q: Why is deflation, meaning generally falling prices, also seen as a danger to the economy?
a: People put off purchases, and the economy can shrink
Because interest rates jump to 20% at once
129491.e: If you expect lower prices, you wait to buy. Companies sell less and may cut jobs.
129491.m: Falling prices can do harm too.

129492.q: What does indirect amortisation of a mortgage mean?
a: You pay into pillar 3a and later use it to pay off the debt
You never pay the mortgage back
The bank pays the mortgage for you
You pay back directly to the bank every month
129492.e: Instead of reducing the debt directly, you save in pillar 3a. The mortgage, and so the deductible interest, stays the same for the time being.

129493.q: A fixed-rate mortgage is coming to an end. What risk do the owners face?
a: The new mortgage may have a higher interest rate
The house then belongs to the bank
129493.e: When renewing, the current interest rate applies. If it has risen, housing costs rise too.
129493.m: On renewal, the new rate counts.

129494.q: After her apprenticeship Lea earns much more. What helps her still save well?
a: Raising her savings straight away and not increasing her spending to the same extent
Taking out a loan for a car
129494.e: With higher pay, spending often rises too. If you save part of the increase straight away, you hardly notice going without.

129495.q: One yoghurt costs 1 franc. A pack of 6 of the same yoghurts costs 5 francs. Which is cheaper per yoghurt?
129495.e: 6 single yoghurts cost 6 francs. The pack costs only 5 francs. But it is only worth it if you eat them all.
129495.m: Only buy big packs if you need everything.

129496.q: Ida only goes ice skating once each winter. Why is it better for her to hire the skates?
a: For one time, hiring costs less than buying
Because she can keep the skates
129496.e: Things you rarely need are often cheaper to hire or borrow than to buy.

129497.q: An unknown online shop has only glowing reviews, all in similar words. What is smart?
a: Be suspicious, the reviews could be fake
129497.e: Reviews can be bought or made up. Independent sources and warning lists help you judge a shop.
129497.m: Reviews that are too perfect are suspicious.

129498.q: Someone offers you money to have parcels delivered to your address and then send them on. What is true?
a: This is often fraud, and you can become an accomplice
This is a safe side job
This is normal at Swiss Post
This is allowed if you do not look inside
129498.e: Often the goods were ordered with stolen card details. Anyone who forwards them is helping the fraudsters.
129498.m: Do not forward other people’s parcels.

129499.q: Why should your bank card PIN not be the same as your phone code?
a: Anyone who spies one code would then know both
Because otherwise the card does not work
Because otherwise the phone gets slower
Because the bank checks this every day
129499.e: If your phone and card are stolen together, the thief would have access to both straight away with one code.
129499.m: Different codes for card and phone.

a: A cryptocurrency whose value is meant to be tied to a currency such as the dollar
A savings account with fixed interest
129500.e: Stablecoins are meant to fluctuate less than other cryptocurrencies. But they are not protected by deposit insurance.
129500.m: Stablecoins are tied to a currency, but not risk-free.

129501.q: What does a share’s price-to-earnings ratio show?
a: How many years’ earnings per share the share price corresponds to
How much dividend is paid out
How high the bank’s fee is
129501.e: You divide the price by the earnings per share. A high ratio means the share is expensive compared with its earnings.
129501.m: P/E ratio = price divided by earnings per share.

a: An investment issued by a bank with a fixed term and fixed interest
A bill from the health insurer
A share of the National Bank
129502.e: With a medium-term note you lend the bank money for a few years. In return you get a fixed interest rate.
129502.m: Medium-term note: fixed interest, fixed term.

129503.q: Lina asks: “Is the mayor allowed to keep the tax money for himself?” What is true?
a: No, it is for tasks that serve everyone
Yes, if he works a lot
No, it belongs to the bank
129503.e: Tax money belongs to the public. The municipality has to spend it on school, roads and other shared tasks.
129503.m: Tax money is money from everyone for everyone.

129504.q: In many villages, where do the people who look after the municipality work?
129504.e: The municipal building houses the municipality’s offices, for example the residents’ registration office or the tax office.
129504.m: The municipality has its offices in the municipal building.

129505.q: Who leads the municipality in many Swiss villages?
129505.e: At the head of the municipality there is usually a mayor, called the municipal president. They lead the municipal council.
129505.m: The municipality is led by the mayor.

129506.q: Who checks that restaurants cook cleanly and safely?
129506.e: Experts from the canton check kitchens and food. Their work is paid for with tax money and protects everyone.

129507.q: What is the building in Bern called where the Swiss Parliament meets?
129507.e: The National Council and the Council of States debate in the Federal Palace in Bern. The Confederation’s money is also decided on there.
129507.m: Parliament meets in the Federal Palace in Bern.

129508.q: New traffic lights are put up at a crossroads. Who usually pays for them?
129508.e: Traffic lights are part of the roads. These are built and maintained by the municipality or canton with tax money.
129508.m: The state pays for traffic lights with taxes.

129509.q: A dam against flooding is being built by the stream. Where does the money for it come from?
a: From the fish in the stream
129509.e: Flood protection protects many houses and people. That is why the municipality, canton and Confederation pay for it with tax money.
129509.m: Protection against natural hazards is paid for with taxes.

129510.q: In the mountains there are avalanche barriers made of wood and steel. Who helps pay for them?
a: The Confederation, canton and municipality with taxes
Only the cows on the alpine pasture
129510.e: Avalanche barriers protect villages and roads. Because many people benefit from them, the state pays with tax money.
129510.m: The state pays for avalanche protection with taxes.

129511.q: Lea learns the recorder at music school. Why do the lessons often cost less than they really cost?
a: Because the municipality pays part of it
Because the teacher gets no pay
129511.e: Many municipalities support the music school with tax money. That way more children can learn an instrument.
129511.m: The municipality often contributes to the music school.

129512.q: Tim lives far from the school and takes the school bus. Who usually pays for the school bus?
129512.e: The municipality has to make sure all children get to school safely. It pays for the school bus with tax money.
129512.m: The municipality usually pays for the school bus.

129513.q: A police officer comes to your class and practises crossing the road safely with you. Who pays her wages?
129513.e: The police are paid with taxes. Road safety lessons at school are also part of their job.
129513.m: The police are paid with taxes.

129514.q: Your mum gets you a new identity card and pays for it at the office. What is a payment like this called?
129514.e: For a particular service from an office you pay a fee. Here the service is the new identity card.
129514.m: For a service from an office you pay a fee.

129515.q: In winter the village has an ice rink with cheap entry. Who often helps pay for it?
129515.e: Many municipalities contribute to ice rinks, swimming pools and sports grounds. That is why entry is cheaper.
129515.m: Sports facilities are often partly paid for by the municipality.

129516.q: The football pitch next to the school gets new grass. Who usually pays for this?
129516.e: Sports pitches at schools usually belong to the municipality. It pays for their upkeep with tax money.
129516.m: The municipality pays for school sports pitches.

129517.q: Granny no longer works because she is retired. Where does she get money from every month?
a: Money from the tax office as a present
129517.e: In Switzerland, people who are retired get a pension from the AHV (old-age insurance). Granny paid contributions from her wages for this in the past.
129517.m: In old age you get an AHV pension.

129518.q: From what age do people in Switzerland normally get their AHV pension?
129518.e: The normal retirement age for the AHV is 65, for women and men.
129518.m: The AHV pension normally starts at 65.

129519.q: Every month some of Dad’s wages go to the AHV. What is this money used for?
129519.e: The pensions of retired people are paid with the AHV contributions of working people. Later Dad will get a pension himself.
129519.m: AHV contributions pay older people’s pensions.

129520.q: Customs officers work at the border. Who pays their wages?
129520.e: Customs is a task of the Confederation, because the border affects the whole of Switzerland.

129521.q: Three families each put 10 francs into a shared fund. How much money is in it?
129521.e: 3 times 10 francs is 30 francs. Taxes work like this too: many people give something, and together it adds up to a lot.
129521.m: Many small amounts add up to a lot.

129522.q: A municipality has 100 francs. It spends 60 francs on the school. How much is left?
129522.e: 100 minus 60 makes 40 francs. A municipality also has to work out what its money will stretch to.

129523.q: The adults vote on whether the municipality should build a new school building. Most say yes. What is it built with?
129523.e: When the voters say yes, the municipality may spend the money. It comes from taxes.
129523.m: After a yes vote, the municipality spends tax money.

129524.q: A car is parked in the wrong place and gets a ticket with an amount on it. What is this money called?
129524.e: A fine is a punishment because you did not keep to a rule. A tax, on the other hand, you pay even if you have done nothing wrong.

129525.q: An old sofa is broken and has to go. What do many municipalities charge to collect it?
a: Nothing at all, you put it in the woods
129525.e: For large waste such as furniture, many municipalities charge a bulky waste fee, for example with a sticker. Leaving it outdoors is forbidden.
129525.m: You often pay a fee for bulky waste.

129526.q: What is a tax, simply explained?
a: Money you give the state for shared tasks
Money you get back in a shop
129526.e: With taxes, everyone together pays for things like schools, roads and the police.
129526.m: Taxes are money for shared tasks.

129527.q: Is your neighbour allowed to demand taxes from you?
a: No, only the state may demand taxes
Yes, if he has a house
129527.e: Only the municipality, canton and Confederation may demand taxes, and only if a law allows it.
129527.m: Only the state may demand taxes.

129528.q: A road sweeper cleans the town’s streets at night. Who pays for it?
a: The children who eat ice cream
129528.e: Clean streets are a task of the municipality. It pays for the machines and staff with tax money.
129528.m: The municipality pays for street cleaning.

129529.q: There is an old fountain in the village. Who usually looks after it?
129529.e: Public fountains usually belong to the municipality. It makes sure they are clean and running.
129529.m: The municipality looks after public fountains.

129530.q: Children eat together at the school lunch club. Who often pays for it?
a: The parents pay part and the municipality contributes
The children alone with pocket money
129530.e: Often the parents pay a contribution. The municipality supports the lunch club with tax money.
129530.m: The municipality often contributes to the lunch club.

129531.q: Who owns the SBB, the Swiss Federal Railways?
129531.e: The SBB belongs to the Confederation, so to the whole of Switzerland. That is why it is called the Federal Railways.
129531.m: The SBB belongs to the Confederation.

129532.q: Who puts up the road signs by the road?
129532.e: Road signs are part of the road. The municipality or canton puts them up and pays for them with taxes.
129532.m: The state pays for road signs.

129533.q: What is the place called where the municipality keeps its vehicles and tools for roads and squares?
129533.e: The people who look after roads, squares and parks for the municipality work at the municipal depot.
129533.m: The municipal workers have their depot.

129534.q: In Switzerland, where does the dustcart usually take the rubbish from the bin bags?
129534.e: Burnable rubbish is incinerated in Switzerland. The heat is often used for heating or electricity.
129534.m: Rubbish is burnt in the incineration plant.

129535.q: Why does a family save money if it collects glass, aluminium and paper separately?
a: It needs fewer bin bags with a fee
It gets wages from the municipality
It no longer has to pay taxes
Glass is then free in shops
129535.e: The fee is included in the price of the bin bags. If you separate well, you fill fewer bags and pay less.
129535.m: If you separate rubbish, you pay less bag fee.

129536.q: Do retired people pay taxes too?
a: Only if they have a bike
129536.e: A pension is income too. So retired people also pay taxes if their income is high enough.

129537.q: The village has a new skate park for all young people. Who probably paid for it?
129537.e: Public facilities for everyone are usually paid for by the municipality with taxes.
129537.m: The municipality pays for public facilities.

129538.q: What is the difference between a donation and a tax?
a: A donation is voluntary, a tax must be paid
129538.e: You give donations voluntarily, for example to a charity. Taxes are compulsory for everyone who earns enough.
129538.m: Donations are voluntary, taxes are compulsory.

129539.q: Mr Weber does not feel like paying taxes. Can he simply choose not to?
129539.e: Paying taxes is required by law. Anyone who does not pay gets reminders and still has to pay in the end.

129540.q: An adult forgets to pay the tax bill. What do they usually get then?
129540.e: A reminder is a letter that reminds you of the unpaid bill. Often interest is added as well.
129540.m: If you do not pay, you get a reminder.

129541.q: The municipality builds two playgrounds. Each costs 5000 francs. How much do both cost together?
129541.e: 2 times 5000 francs is 10,000 francs. The money comes from taxes.

129542.q: The Meier family needs 20 francs’ worth of bin bags a month, the Huber family separates more and only needs 10 francs’ worth. How much less does the Huber family pay?
129542.e: 20 minus 10 makes 10 francs. If you have less rubbish, you pay a lower fee.
129542.m: Less rubbish means a lower fee.

129543.q: Many municipalities have a tax on dogs. Is there also a cat tax in Switzerland?
a: Yes, but only for black cats
129543.e: In Switzerland there is a dog tax, but no cat tax.
129543.m: Dog tax yes, cat tax no.

129544.q: A family has no more money for food and rent. Who helps them in Switzerland?
a: The tax office with a fine
129544.e: People who do not have enough money to live on get help from social assistance. It is paid for with tax money.
129544.m: Social assistance helps people in need.

129545.q: Lukas says: “The playground in the park is free.” What is more accurate?
a: There is no entry fee, but taxes pay for it
Nobody ever paid anything for it
Lukas has to pay every time
129545.e: You pay nothing to use it. But the playground is built and looked after with everyone’s tax money.
129545.m: Free for you means paid for by everyone.

129546.q: Why do adults write the truth in their tax return?
a: Because it is compulsory and fair to everyone
Because otherwise they win a prize
129546.e: If you state honestly how much you earn, you pay the right share. Anyone who cheats is unfair to everyone else and is punished.
129546.m: The truth belongs in your tax return.

129547.q: When do many parents sit down to do their tax return?
a: In spring, for the previous year
At Christmas, for the next year
Only on the beach in the summer holidays
129547.e: In many cantons the tax return must be handed in by the end of March. It covers the year before.
129547.m: The tax return is often done in spring.

129548.q: In the past, farmers had to hand over part of their harvest. What was this old levy called?
129548.e: With the tithe, farmers handed over about a tenth of their harvest, for example to the Church. So levies have existed for a very long time.
129548.m: The tithe was an old levy.

129549.e: Swiss Post belongs to the Confederation. It makes sure letters and parcels arrive all over Switzerland.
129549.m: Swiss Post belongs to the Confederation.

129550.q: The big road between two villages is called a cantonal road. Who is responsible for it?
129550.e: Cantonal roads link villages and towns. The canton builds and maintains them with tax money.
129550.m: Cantonal roads belong to the canton.

129551.q: There is a hole in the small residential street in front of your house. Who usually repairs it?
129551.e: Small residential streets are usually municipal roads. The municipality repairs them.
129551.m: The municipality looks after residential streets.

129552.q: Mum works in an office. What is the money she gets every month for her work called?
129552.e: If you are employed and work, you get wages. Later you also pay taxes on these wages.

a: Money you get regularly in old age
A punishment for driving too fast
129553.e: People who are retired get a pension every month, for example from the AHV.
129553.m: A pension is money for old age.

129554.q: Who pays money into the AHV?
a: Nobody, the money comes by itself
129554.e: AHV contributions are deducted from wages, and the employer pays the same amount on top. That is how the pensions come about.
129554.m: Workers and employers pay into the AHV.

129555.q: Does all of Dad’s pay go into his bank account?
a: No, contributions such as for the AHV are deducted first
Yes, and a bit more on top
129555.e: Contributions for the AHV and other insurance are taken from the pay. What is left goes into the account.
129555.m: Contributions are taken from your pay.

129556.q: The weather forecast often comes from MeteoSwiss. Who pays for MeteoSwiss?
129556.e: MeteoSwiss is a federal office. It is paid for with tax money and warns the whole of Switzerland about severe weather.

129557.q: The National Museum in Zurich shows the history of Switzerland. Who mainly pays for it?
129557.e: The National Museum is part of the Confederation’s Swiss National Museum. Most of it is paid for with tax money.
129557.m: The Confederation pays for the National Museum.

129558.q: Who decides how much tax adults have to pay?
a: Laws decided on by Parliament and the people
The tax office as it pleases
129558.e: Taxes are set out in laws. These are passed by Parliament and often by the people at the ballot box too.
129558.m: Taxes are laid down in laws.

129559.q: What does the tax office do?
a: It calculates taxes and collects them
It sells steering wheels for cars
129559.e: The tax office checks tax returns, works out how much someone has to pay and sends the bill.

129560.q: Do farming families in Switzerland get money from the Confederation?
a: Yes, for example for looking after the landscape
129560.e: The Confederation pays farmers direct payments, for example for well-kept meadows and good animal husbandry. The money comes from taxes.
129560.m: Farmers get direct payments from the Confederation.

129561.q: In winter the classroom is nice and warm. Who pays for heating the school building?
129561.e: The school building usually belongs to the municipality. It pays for heating, electricity and cleaning with tax money.

129562.q: Who pays the caretaker who repairs and tidies up in the school?
129562.e: The caretaker works for the municipality. His wages are paid with tax money.

129563.q: Rega rescues people by helicopter. Where does it get a large part of its money from?
129563.e: Rega is a foundation. Many people voluntarily pay a patron’s contribution every year. Not everything important is paid for with taxes.

129564.q: The Keller family gets a bill for the water from the tap. What are they paying for with it?
129564.e: You pay a fee for drinking water. If you use more water, you pay more.
129564.m: You pay a fee for drinking water.

129565.q: In the village, 10 families each give 100 francs for a new piece of play equipment. How much money is collected?
129565.e: 10 times 100 francs is 1000 francs. Together you can afford more than alone.
129565.m: Together a lot of money comes together.

129566.q: A school trip costs 20 francs per child. The municipality pays half. How much does each child still pay?
129566.e: Half of 20 francs is 10 francs. The municipality covers this part, the parents pay the rest.

129567.q: Switzerland is divided into cantons. What is a canton?
a: A part of Switzerland with its own government and laws
A small village without a school
129567.e: Each canton has its own government, a parliament and its own taxes. Each canton has many municipalities.
129567.m: A canton is a part of Switzerland with its own government.

129568.q: What is the town called where a canton’s government works?
129568.e: Each canton has a capital, for example Aarau in Aargau or Chur in the Grisons.

129569.q: Does every Swiss municipality belong to a canton?
129569.e: Every municipality is in a canton. That is why people pay taxes to the municipality, canton and Confederation.
129569.m: Every municipality belongs to a canton.

129570.q: Which level lies between the municipality and the Confederation?
129570.e: From small to big: municipality, canton, Confederation. All three have their own tasks and their own taxes.
129570.m: Municipality, canton, Confederation: from small to big.

129571.q: Tourists from Japan buy chocolate in Lucerne. Do they pay VAT too?
a: Yes, it is included in the price
129571.e: VAT is included in the price. Anyone who shops in Switzerland pays it, wherever they come from.
129571.m: Everyone who shops here pays VAT.

129572.q: The PostBus also goes to small mountain villages where only a few people get on. How is that possible?
a: The Confederation and canton contribute tax money
129572.e: With few passengers, the tickets would not be enough. The Confederation and canton pay part so that mountain villages are connected too.
129572.m: Thanks to taxes, even small villages have a PostBus.

129573.q: Studying at a university costs a lot. Who pays most of it?
a: The canton and Confederation with tax money
The students entirely on their own
129573.e: Students pay tuition fees, but these only cover a small part. The canton and Confederation pay the rest.
129573.m: Universities are mainly paid for with taxes.

129574.q: Grass cuttings and vegetable peelings go in the green waste container. What do many municipalities charge for this?
a: A fee, often with a sticker
Nothing at all, you throw it in the stream
129574.e: Many municipalities charge a fee for green waste collection. You stick a sticker on the container, for example.
129574.m: You often pay a fee for green waste too.

129575.q: What do people mean when they talk about “the state”?
a: The municipality, canton and Confederation together
129575.e: “The state” means all public levels that take on tasks for everyone and collect taxes.
129575.m: The state is the municipality, canton and Confederation.

129576.q: The grass along the edge of the cantonal road is mown. Who pays for this?
129576.e: The roadside is part of the cantonal road. The canton looks after it with tax money.
129576.m: The canton looks after its roads.

129577.q: Where do judges help settle a dispute?
129577.e: Courts decide disputes according to the law. They are part of the state and are paid for with taxes.
129577.m: Courts settle disputes according to the law.

129578.q: Apart from their training company, apprentices also go to vocational school. Who mainly pays for it?
129578.e: Vocational schools are mainly paid for by the canton with tax money.
129578.m: The canton pays for vocational school.

129579.q: By the road there is a hydrant from which the fire brigade gets water. Who makes sure it works?
129579.e: Hydrants are part of the municipal water supply. That way the fire brigade has water for firefighting everywhere.

129580.q: In the holidays there is a holiday pass with courses and trips. Who often helps pay for it?
129580.e: Many holiday passes are organised by municipalities and clubs and supported with the municipality’s money.
129580.m: The municipality often supports the holiday pass.

129581.q: The receipt says “incl. VAT”. What does “incl.” mean?
a: Including, the tax is already in it
The tax is added on top
129581.e: “Incl.” is short for “including”. So the VAT is already included in the price.

129582.q: Mia finds a purse in the street. Where can she take it in many municipalities?
a: To the lost property office or the police
To the tax office as tax
129582.e: Found items are handed in at the lost property office or to the police. That way they can be returned to their owners.
129582.m: Found items belong at the lost property office.

129583.q: The Rossi family moves to a new village. Where do they have to register?
a: With the municipality, at the residents’ registration office
With the Federal Council in Bern
129583.e: When you move, you register with the new municipality. That way it knows who lives there and who has to pay taxes.
129583.m: After moving, you register with the municipality.

129584.q: Big cities often have their own police. What are they called?
129584.e: As well as the cantonal police, some cities have a city police force. It is paid for by the city with taxes.
129584.m: Big cities often have city police.

129585.q: Who makes the franc coins in Switzerland?
129585.e: The coins are minted by the federal mint in Bern. Money is a task of the Confederation.

129586.q: At the bus stop there is a shelter with a roof and a bench. Who usually pays for it?
129586.e: Bus stops are often built and looked after by the municipality. The money comes from taxes.
129586.m: The municipality often looks after bus stops.

129587.q: Who gets the money when someone pays a fine?
a: The state, for example the municipality or canton
129587.e: Fines go to the state. They are a punishment and not a reward for the police.

129588.q: The municipality divides 100 francs equally between two playgrounds. How much does each playground get?
129588.e: 100 divided by 2 makes 50. The municipality has to share its money fairly.

a: A person who gives taxes away
129589.e: Everyone who pays taxes is called a taxpayer. The state pays for its tasks with their money.
129589.m: Someone who pays taxes is a taxpayer.

129590.q: The municipality gets money from taxes. What is money coming in called?
129590.e: Income is all the money that comes in. For the municipality, that is mainly taxes.

129591.q: The municipality pays for teachers, roads and playgrounds. What is this money called?
129591.e: Expenses are the money that goes out. The municipality should not spend more than it takes in.

129592.q: What happens if a municipality spends more than it takes in?
a: It has to borrow money and has debts
129592.e: If money is missing, the municipality has to borrow it. It must pay borrowed money back later with interest.
129592.m: Spending more than you take in creates debt.

129593.q: Why does a municipality sometimes put money aside?
a: For big expenses later, such as a new school building
Because it does not like the money
So nobody pays taxes any more
129593.e: Big buildings cost a lot. If you save beforehand, you need less debt later.
129593.m: A municipality also saves for later.

129594.q: At the edge of the woods there is a public fireplace with wood for everyone. Who often provides it?
a: The municipality or the forestry service
129594.e: Public fireplaces are often built and looked after by the municipality or the forestry service.
129594.m: The municipality often looks after public fireplaces.

129595.q: Parents get an amount every month for each child. What is this money called?
129595.e: The child allowance helps families cover the costs of their children. It is usually paid out with the wages.
129595.m: There is a child allowance for children.

129596.q: May the municipality use tax money to pay for a private birthday party for the mayor?
a: No, tax money is for public tasks
129596.e: Tax money may only be spent on tasks that serve everyone. Private parties are not among them.
129596.m: Tax money is for everyone, not for private use.

129597.q: Which of these buildings is a public building?
a: The tree house in the garden
129597.e: Public buildings belong to the state and serve everyone, for example school buildings or the municipal building.

129598.q: Your bike has been stolen and you report it to the police. Do you have to pay for this?
a: No, it is paid for with taxes
129598.e: The work of the police is paid for with taxes. Reporting a theft costs nothing.

129599.q: The Gotthard Base Tunnel is one of the longest railway tunnels in the world. Who mainly paid for it?
129599.e: The Confederation pays for big railway projects for the whole country with taxes and levies.
129599.m: The Confederation pays for big railway tunnels.

129600.q: Why do we need a state with taxes at all?
a: So that tasks for everyone are organised and paid for
So nobody has to work any more
So everyone has the same pocket money
129600.e: Some things everyone needs, but nobody can pay for alone, for example schools, police and roads.
129600.m: The state organises what everyone needs.

129601.q: What is the three-letter insurance that retired people in Switzerland get their pension from?
129601.e: The AHV is the most important insurance for old age. Almost all adults in Switzerland pay contributions to it.
129601.m: The old-age pension comes from the AHV.

129602.q: The teacher is ill and a supply teacher teaches the class. Who pays the supply teacher?
a: The municipality and canton with tax money
129602.e: Teachers at state schools are paid by the municipality and canton. This also applies to supply teachers.
129602.m: The state pays supply teachers too.

a: The pay that goes into your account
129603.e: Gross pay is the agreed pay. Contributions such as AHV and the pension fund are still deducted from it.

129604.q: Lea’s payslip shows gross pay and net pay. Which amount goes into her account?
a: Neither, the money goes to the tax office
129604.e: Net pay is what is left after the deductions. This amount is paid out.
129604.m: Net is what goes into your account.

129605.q: For employees, who pays the contributions to AHV, IV and EO?
129605.e: Half is deducted from the pay, and the employer adds the other half. The employer transfers everything to the compensation office.
129605.m: Employees and employers share AHV contributions.

129606.q: What does the abbreviation ALV on a payslip stand for?
129606.e: Unemployment insurance pays money if you lose your job. The contribution is deducted from your pay.

129607.q: Which three digits does every Swiss AHV number begin with?
129607.e: The AHV number has 13 digits and always begins with 756, the country code for Switzerland.

129608.q: Where can you find your own AHV number, for example?
129608.e: The AHV number is on your health insurance card. You need it, for example, for your first pay.
129608.m: The AHV number is on your health insurance card.

129609.q: From when do working people in Switzerland have to pay AHV contributions?
a: From their first day at school
129609.e: Anyone who works pays AHV contributions from their pay from 1 January after their 17th birthday.
129609.m: AHV contributions from the January after your 17th birthday.

129610.q: Mr Frei keeps 3000 francs in cash at home in a box. Does he have to declare it in his tax return?
a: Yes, as part of his assets
Only if it is in a safe
129610.e: Assets include everything you own, including cash. What counts is the amount on 31 December.
129610.m: Cash is part of your assets too.

129611.q: What does the income compensation scheme (EO) pay money for?
a: As replacement pay during military service and maternity
129611.e: People doing military, civilian or civil protection service, or having a baby, get part of their pay from the EO.
129611.m: The EO replaces pay during service and maternity.

129612.q: What is the difference between a payslip and a salary statement?
a: The payslip comes every month, the salary statement once a year
The salary statement comes every day
The tax office writes the payslip
129612.e: The payslip shows pay and deductions every month. The salary statement sums up the whole year and goes with the tax return.

129613.q: Jonas has a gross pay of 1000 francs. The deductions are 120 francs. What is his net pay?
129613.e: Net pay equals gross pay minus deductions: 1000 minus 120 makes 880 francs.

129614.q: What is the 2nd pillar of retirement provision called, which is also deducted from pay?
129614.e: The pension fund, also called occupational pension provision, adds to the AHV pension in old age. Employees and employers pay into it.
129614.m: The 2nd pillar is the pension fund.

129615.q: Where does the employer transfer the AHV contributions deducted from pay?
129615.e: The compensation offices collect the contributions for AHV, IV and EO and later pay out the pensions.
129615.m: AHV contributions go to the compensation office.

129616.q: Are the AHV contributions taken from pay a tax?
a: No, they are contributions to a social insurance
Yes, they are the municipal tax
Yes, they are the dog tax
129616.e: With AHV contributions you are insured and later get a pension. Taxes, on the other hand, pay for the state’s general tasks.
129616.m: AHV contributions are insurance contributions, not taxes.

129617.q: Is the health insurance premium a tax?
a: No, it is the price of an insurance policy
Yes, it goes to the Confederation
Yes, it is part of VAT
129617.e: You pay the premium to the health insurer for basic insurance. It is compulsory, but it is not a tax.
129617.m: The health insurance premium is not a tax.

129618.q: Who funds child allowances in most cantons?
129618.e: Employers pay contributions to a family compensation fund. This pays out the allowances with the wages.
129618.m: Child allowances are mainly funded by employers.

129619.q: What deduction can parents make for their children in their tax return?
129619.e: Children cost money. That is why parents may deduct a fixed amount per child from their income and pay less tax.
129619.m: There is a tax deduction for children.

129620.q: Do you have to fill in a separate tax return for the municipality, canton and Confederation?
a: No, one tax return covers all three
Yes, and one more for the school
129620.e: You fill in one tax return. From it, the tax office works out the taxes for the municipality, canton and Confederation.
129620.m: One tax return for all three levels.

129621.q: What must on no account be missing from a paper tax return?
129621.e: With your signature you confirm that the information is complete and true.
129621.m: You have to sign your tax return.

129622.q: In many cantons, what can you do if you cannot pay the tax bill all at once?
a: Ask the tax office for payment by instalments
Write less in the tax return
129622.e: If you contact the tax office early, you can often pay in instalments. Ignoring it leads to reminders and interest.
129622.m: With money problems, ask the tax office early.

129623.q: What does the bank send at the start of the year so that you can declare your account in your tax return?
a: A statement with the balance and interest as of 31 December
129623.e: For the tax return you need the balance at the end of the year and the interest. The bank issues a certificate for this.
129623.m: The bank provides the statement for the tax office.

129624.q: Which health insurance document is useful for the tax return?
a: The certificate of premiums and costs paid
A photo of the insurance card
129624.e: Premiums and medical costs you paid yourself can be partly deducted. The health insurer confirms the amounts.
129624.m: The health insurer confirms premiums for tax.

129625.q: What do you need to deduct a donation in your tax return?
a: A donation receipt from the organisation
Nothing, you just write an amount
A letter to the Federal Council
129625.e: The tax office requires proof. Non-profit organisations issue a donation receipt for this.

129626.q: In Switzerland, who mainly awards grants for education and training?
129626.e: If the family cannot pay enough for an education, the cantons help with grants. The money comes from taxes.
129626.m: Grants are mainly awarded by the cantons.

129627.q: Who decides the Confederation’s budget every year?
a: Parliament, that is the National Council and the Council of States
129627.e: The Federal Council proposes the budget, and it is decided by the Federal Assembly made up of the National Council and Council of States.

129628.e: The cantonal parliament, called the Kantonsrat or Grosser Rat depending on the canton, decides on the budget.
129628.m: The cantonal parliament decides the cantonal budget.

129629.q: What does the principle of subsidiarity mean in Switzerland?
a: Whatever a smaller level can do well itself, it does itself
Other countries do all the tasks
Only the municipality may raise taxes
129629.e: Tasks are solved as close to the people as possible, so first in the municipality, then in the canton and only then at federal level.
129629.m: Subsidiarity: as close to the people as possible.

129630.q: What is it called when the Confederation, cantons and municipalities have their own tasks and their own taxes?
129630.e: In federalism, several levels share power. The cantons have a lot of independence.
129630.m: Switzerland is organised on federal lines.

129631.q: In many municipalities, what do adults pay if they do not serve in the fire brigade?
129631.e: Many municipalities have compulsory fire service. Anyone who does not serve pays an exemption levy.
129631.m: Without fire service you often pay an exemption levy.

129632.q: In Switzerland, who generally has to pay the radio and television levy?
a: Every household, even without a TV
Only people who watch TV every day
129632.e: The levy is charged per household, whether or not you own any devices. Only a few exceptions are possible.
129632.m: Every household pays the radio and TV levy.

129633.q: The Graf family is building a garden shed and needs planning permission. What does the municipality charge for it?
129633.e: The municipality checks the planning application. It charges a fee for this work.
129633.m: You pay a fee for planning permission.

129634.q: Jan pays the road traffic office for his learner driver’s permit. What kind of payment is this?
129634.e: Jan receives a particular service from the office for the permit. For this he pays a fee.
129634.m: You pay fees for permits and IDs.

129635.q: In many municipalities, what pays for cleaning waste water?
129635.e: Waste water from households is cleaned in sewage treatment plants. The costs are mainly covered by fees.

129636.q: Besides the bag fee, many municipalities charge a basic fee for rubbish. What for?
a: For fixed costs such as collection points and organisation
For the right to throw rubbish in the woods
For new clothes for the municipal workers
129636.e: Some costs arise however many bags someone uses. These are covered by a basic fee.
129636.m: The basic fee covers fixed rubbish costs.

129637.q: In Switzerland, which level is usually responsible for social assistance?
129637.e: The municipalities pay out social assistance. The canton sets the rules.
129637.m: Social assistance is usually a matter for the municipality.

129638.q: Who pays the premium reduction that helps people with little money with their health insurance?
a: The Confederation and cantons with tax money
129638.e: The Confederation and cantons give tax money so that everyone can afford the compulsory basic insurance.
129638.m: The Confederation and cantons pay premium reductions.

129639.q: Where does a municipality usually get most of its money from?
a: From the taxes of residents and companies
129639.e: The municipalities’ most important income is income, wealth and profit taxes.

a: There is no more money in the world
129640.e: With a deficit, money is missing. It has to be covered with savings or new debt.
129640.m: Deficit means spending more than you took in.

129641.q: A municipality takes in 5 million francs and spends 4 million. What does it have?
129641.e: 5 minus 4 makes 1 million. If you take in more than you spend, you have a surplus.
129641.m: More income than expenses gives a surplus.

129642.q: Why is value added tax called that?
a: At each stage, the value added is taxed
Because it is worth more than other taxes
Because you pay it several times a month
Because it only applies to expensive things
129642.e: From raw material to finished product, value is added at each stage. Exactly this added value is taxed.
129642.m: The value added at each stage is taxed.

129643.q: How must shops in Switzerland show their prices to customers?
129643.e: The displayed price must already include VAT. That way you know what you will pay at the till.

129644.q: How can you tell from an invoice that a company is registered for VAT?
a: By a number with “CHE” and the addition “MWST”
129644.e: Companies have a business identification number beginning with CHE. For companies registered for VAT, “MWST” follows it.
129644.m: VAT-registered companies have a CHE number with MWST.

129645.q: Mia shops abroad and goes over the allowed duty-free limit. What must she do at the Swiss border?
a: Declare the goods and pay Swiss VAT
129645.e: Purchases are tax-free up to a limit. Above it, you must declare the goods at customs and pay Swiss VAT.
129645.m: Above the limit you pay VAT at the border.

129646.q: Which cantonal office checks whether a car is roadworthy?
129646.e: The cantonal road traffic office tests vehicles, issues licences and collects the motor vehicle tax.
129646.m: The road traffic office tests cars.

129647.q: What does the abbreviation AHV stand for?
a: Old-age and survivors’ insurance (Alters- und Hinterlassenenversicherung)
129647.e: The AHV pays pensions in old age and to survivors, for example to children whose father or mother has died.

129648.q: A self-employed hairdresser has no employer. How does she pay her AHV contributions?
a: She pays them herself to the compensation office
Not at all, she is exempt
129648.e: Self-employed people settle directly with the compensation office. They pay the contributions alone, because no employer covers half.
129648.m: Self-employed people pay the AHV themselves.

a: Work that is not reported, without AHV contributions or taxes
129649.e: With undeclared work, pay and work are hidden from the authorities. This is forbidden.
129649.m: Undeclared work is forbidden, hidden work.

129650.q: Why is undeclared work also bad for the person doing it?
a: They are not insured and have gaps in their AHV
They then get too much pension
They have to sleep twice as long
They may never have a holiday again
129650.e: Without registration, contributions to the AHV and accident insurance are missing. Then there is no protection in an accident or in old age.
129650.m: Undeclared work also harms your own provision.

129651.q: Which of these must be declared as income in the tax return?
a: The value of a chestnut you found
129651.e: Pensions from the AHV and the pension fund are income and must be taxed.

129652.q: The payslip shows a deduction “NBU”. What does it stand for?
129652.e: NBU insures accidents in your free time. Anyone who works at least 8 hours a week for the same employer is covered by it.
129652.m: NBU insures accidents in your free time.

129653.q: Nina is 16 and starts her apprenticeship in August. Are AHV contributions already deducted from her pay?
a: Not yet, only from the January after her 17th birthday
Only if she earns more than her boss
129653.e: The AHV obligation for working people starts on 1 January after their 17th birthday. Before that, no AHV contributions are deducted.
129653.m: At 16 you do not yet pay AHV contributions.

129654.q: Which taxes are higher for most people in Switzerland: cantonal and municipal tax together, or direct federal tax?
a: Both are always exactly the same
129654.e: For most incomes, direct federal tax is only a smaller part. Most goes to the canton and municipality.
129654.m: Most income tax goes to the canton and municipality.

129655.q: In the past in Switzerland, who often received the farmers’ tithe?
129655.e: In the Middle Ages and long afterwards, farmers handed a tenth of their harvest to the Church or to landlords.
129655.m: The tithe went to the Church or landlords.

129656.q: Since which year has the AHV existed in Switzerland?
129656.e: The people approved the AHV in 1947. Pensions have been paid since 1 January 1948.

129657.q: Since which year has VAT existed in Switzerland?
129657.e: VAT was introduced on 1 January 1995. It replaced the earlier turnover tax on goods.

129658.q: Which tax existed in Switzerland before VAT?
129658.e: Until 1994 there was the turnover tax on goods. In 1995 it was replaced by VAT.
129658.m: Before VAT there was the WUST.

129659.q: What was direct federal tax called in the past?
129659.e: It was introduced in the Second World War to fund national defence, which is why it was called defence tax. It was renamed later.
129659.m: Direct federal tax used to be called defence tax.

129660.q: In many municipalities, who checks whether the municipality has accounted for its money correctly?
129660.e: Elected members check the municipality’s accounts and report to the voters.
129660.m: The municipal accounts are checked by a committee.

129661.q: Which office checks whether the Confederation uses its money correctly and economically?
129661.e: The Swiss Federal Audit Office is the Confederation’s supreme financial supervisory body. It works independently.
129661.m: The Federal Audit Office checks federal spending.

129662.q: The budget is the plan. What does a municipality’s annual accounts show?
a: What was really taken in and spent
What it wants to spend next year
How many children are at school
129662.e: After the year, the accounts are settled. The annual accounts show whether the budget was kept to.
129662.m: The budget is the plan, the accounts are the result.

129663.q: What is an investment by a municipality?
a: Spending on something long-lasting, like a school building
The teachers’ wages for one month
The paper in the municipal building
The fine for parking in the wrong place
129663.e: Investments are large expenses that are useful for many years, such as buildings, roads or pipes.
129663.m: Investments are useful for many years.

129664.q: When do most taxpayers receive the documents for their tax return?
a: At the start of the year
129664.e: The tax office usually sends documents or login details at the start of the year for the previous year.
129664.m: Tax documents arrive at the start of the year.

129665.q: Mr Bühler leaves the Church. What then applies to church tax?
a: As a private individual he no longer has to pay church tax
He has to pay twice as much
He has to pay it to a different church
129665.e: Church tax is paid by members of a national church. Anyone who leaves is exempt from it as a private individual.
129665.m: No church membership, no church tax.

129666.q: Where does a large part of the net profit of Swisslos and Loterie Romande go?
a: To charitable purposes such as culture, sport and social causes
129666.e: The lottery companies give their net profits to the cantons. These use them to support charitable projects.
129666.m: Lottery profits help culture, sport and social causes.

129667.q: Anyone who wants to rent a flat often needs an extract from the debt enforcement register. What do you pay for it?
129667.e: The debt enforcement office issues the extract and charges a fee for it.
129667.m: The debt enforcement extract costs a fee.

129668.q: The dog tax is called a tax. Why is it not a fee?
a: You do not get a specific service in return
129668.e: A fee pays for a specific service. You pay the dog tax simply because you keep a dog, with no direct service in return.
129668.m: Tax: no direct service in return.

129669.q: In many cantons with lakes, boat owners pay a levy to the canton every year. What is it called?
129669.e: Just as for cars, there is an annual cantonal tax for boats.
129669.m: There is a boat tax for boats.

129670.q: A company has sales of 500,000 francs and costs of 400,000 francs. How big is its profit?
129670.e: Profit equals income minus costs: 500,000 minus 400,000 makes 100,000 francs. The company pays profit tax on the profit.

129671.q: In tax law, what is a company such as a public limited company called?
129671.e: Companies such as an AG or GmbH are legal persons. They pay taxes themselves, for example on their profit.
129671.m: An AG is a legal person.

129672.q: In tax law, what is an individual human being called?
129672.e: Human beings are natural persons. They pay, for example, income and wealth tax.
129672.m: A human being is a natural person.

129673.q: Who can help fill in the tax return for a fee?
a: A fiduciary or a tax adviser
129673.e: Fiduciary offices and tax advisers fill in tax returns professionally. But the taxpayer remains responsible for correct information.
129673.m: Fiduciaries help with the tax return for a fee.

129674.q: Do cantons have a tax multiplier too?
a: Yes, many cantons set their own tax multiplier
129674.e: In many cantons the basic tax is multiplied both by the canton’s tax multiplier and by the municipality’s.
129674.m: Many cantons also have a tax multiplier.

129675.q: How can you find out how much tax you would pay in another municipality?
a: With a calculator and no information
129675.e: The Federal Tax Administration and many cantons offer tax calculators. You can use them to compare municipalities.

129676.q: In many shops abroad, what can you ask for to get the local VAT back?
129676.e: With an export form stamped by customs you get the foreign VAT back. Above the duty-free limit you pay Swiss VAT instead.
129676.m: With the export form you get foreign VAT back.

129677.q: What does anyone risk who puts their rubbish out on the street without an official fee bag?
129677.e: Anyone who avoids the bag fee breaks the municipality’s waste rules and can be fined.
129677.m: Rubbish without a fee bag can mean a fine.

129678.q: Why do small municipalities in Switzerland sometimes merge into a bigger municipality?
a: To carry out tasks together better and more cheaply
Because the Confederation orders it every year
So nobody pays taxes any more
Because otherwise they may not have children
129678.e: Small municipalities often find it hard to get staff and can hardly afford expensive tasks alone. A merger can help.
129678.m: Municipalities merge to solve tasks together.

129679.q: Several municipalities run a sewage treatment plant together. What is an association like this called?
129679.e: In a special-purpose association, municipalities work together on a particular task and share the costs.
129679.m: A special-purpose association shares tasks among municipalities.

129680.q: Mrs Imhof’s basic tax is 2000 francs, the municipal tax multiplier is 90 per cent. How much is her municipal tax?
129680.e: 90 per cent of 2000 francs is 1800 francs. A tax multiplier below 100 per cent makes the tax smaller.
129680.m: Tax equals basic tax times tax multiplier.

129681.q: A shop sells a game for 50 francs. This includes 4 francs of VAT. How much of the selling price does the shop keep?
129681.e: The shop has to pass the 4 francs of VAT on to the Confederation. 50 minus 4 makes 46 francs.
129681.m: The VAT in the price belongs to the Confederation.

129682.q: Lea earns 1200 francs a month and gets 12 monthly salaries. Roughly what is on her salary statement for the year?
129682.e: 12 times 1200 makes 14,400 francs. The salary statement shows the pay for the whole year.
129682.m: The salary statement shows the annual pay.

a: An extra month’s pay per year, often in December
The pay for the month of Thirteenber
A present that is not taxed
129683.e: Many employers pay a 13th month’s salary. It is part of income and is taxed like the rest of the pay.
129683.m: The 13th month’s salary is taxed too.

129684.q: Lea gets interest on her savings account. What applies for tax?
a: Interest is income and belongs in the tax return
Interest must be given back to the bank
129684.e: Interest on accounts is income from assets. It is declared in the tax return.

129685.q: Who decides where houses may be built in a village?
129685.e: With the zoning plan, the municipality decides where people may live, work or not build. The canton has to approve the plan.
129685.m: Local planning decides where you may build.

129686.q: Who runs most courts in Switzerland?
129686.e: Most courts, for example district and high courts, are cantonal. The Confederation mainly has the Federal Supreme Court.

129687.q: Who in Switzerland is responsible for relations with other countries?
129687.e: Foreign policy concerns the whole country. That is why the Confederation is responsible.

129688.q: A couple live together but are not married. How do they fill in their tax return?
a: Each person fills in their own
They do not fill one in at all
Only the older person fills one in
129688.e: Unmarried couples are taxed separately. Each person submits their own tax return.
129688.m: Unmarried people each fill in a tax return.

129689.q: Marco works for two employers. How many salary statements does he get for the year?
129689.e: Each employer issues its own salary statement. Marco has to attach both to his tax return.
129689.m: Each employer gives a salary statement.

129690.q: Who elects the members of the parliament that decides on tax laws?
129690.e: The voters elect parliament. It passes tax laws, which the people can often vote on too.

129691.q: From what age can you vote at federal level in Switzerland, for example on VAT?
129691.e: At federal level, Swiss citizens can vote from the age of 18.
129691.m: You can vote at federal level from 18.

129692.q: In which canton can 16-year-olds already vote on cantonal matters, such as taxes?
129692.e: In 2007 Glarus became the first canton to introduce a voting age of 16 at cantonal and municipal level.
129692.m: In Glarus you can vote from 16.

129693.q: In which cantons do voters still vote at an open-air Landsgemeinde, including on taxes?
129693.e: At the Landsgemeinde people vote by raising their hands. This tradition still exists today in Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden.
129693.m: Landsgemeinden exist in Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden.

129694.q: A tradesman writes on the bill “200 francs plus VAT”. What does that mean?
a: VAT is added to the 200 francs
VAT is included in the 200 francs
You do not have to pay any VAT
The tradesman pays the VAT himself
129694.e: “Plus” means added on. On bills to companies, the price is often given without VAT and the tax is added.
129694.m: Plus VAT means it is added on.

129695.q: Why do some till receipts show two different VAT rates?
a: A lower rate applies to food than to other goods
Because the shop made a mistake
129695.e: Food, books and medicines have a reduced rate. If you also buy other things, two rates appear.
129695.m: Food has a lower VAT rate.

129696.q: Why is it worth looking carefully at your own salary statement?
a: Mistakes on it can lead to the wrong taxes
Because otherwise you have to give it back
Because you can win the lottery with it
129696.e: The tax office takes the figures from the salary statement. If something is wrong, you should ask your employer to correct it.

129697.q: In Switzerland, who usually gets the money from the dog tax?
129697.e: The dog tax is usually charged by the municipality where you live, often based on a cantonal law.
129697.m: The dog tax usually goes to the municipality.

129698.q: What is the money from the tourist tax usually used for?
a: For things for guests, such as hiking trails or events
129698.e: Guests pay the tourist tax when they stay overnight. The resort uses it to fund things that mainly benefit guests.

129699.q: Mr Moser will soon be 65. What does he have to do to get his AHV pension?
a: Apply for the pension at the compensation office
Nothing, it always comes by itself
Fill in a new federal tax return
Make a request at the municipal assembly
129699.e: The AHV pension does not come automatically. You apply for it at the compensation office a few months before retirement age.
129699.m: You have to apply for the AHV pension.
