129700.q: What does the expression “the public purse” mean?
a: The state, with the Confederation, cantons and municipalities
129700.e: When something is paid for from the public purse, the money comes from the state, so usually from taxes.
129700.m: The public purse means the state.

129701.q: Who levies gift taxes in Switzerland?
129701.e: Like inheritance tax, gift tax is a matter for the cantons. The Confederation does not levy one.

129702.q: Who pays for Swiss embassies abroad?
129702.e: Embassies represent the whole of Switzerland. They belong to the Confederation’s Department of Foreign Affairs.

129703.q: What does the principle of legality require in tax law?
a: Taxes need a basis in a law
The tax office may set taxes freely
Taxes are only allowed for companies
Taxes must stay the same every year
129703.e: Who is liable to tax, what is taxed and roughly how high the tax is must be set out in law. This protects against arbitrariness.

129704.q: According to which principle of the Federal Constitution should people be taxed?
a: According to the alphabetical order of their name
Everyone pays exactly the same amount
129704.e: The Federal Constitution requires taxes to be based on economic capacity. Those who have more can contribute more.
129704.m: Taxation is based on ability to pay.

129705.q: What does the principle of universality of taxation mean?
a: Everyone in the same situation is taxed, with no privileges for individuals
Only the general body of companies pays taxes
129705.e: Tax laws apply to everyone. Particular groups may not be favoured without an objective reason.
129705.m: Taxes apply to everyone, without privileges.

129706.q: What does the Federal Constitution forbid between cantons?
a: The same income being taxed by two cantons
Cantons raising any taxes at all
129706.e: Intercantonal double taxation is forbidden. If someone has income or assets in several cantons, it is divided up.
129706.m: No income is taxed by two cantons.

129707.q: In tax law, what is the taxable person (Steuersubjekt)?
a: The person who owes the tax
129707.e: The taxable person is whoever is liable to tax, that is a natural or legal person.

129708.q: In income tax, what is the object of taxation?
a: The salary statement as a piece of paper
129708.e: The object of taxation is what is taxed. For income tax it is income, for wealth tax it is wealth.
129708.m: Object of taxation: what is taxed.

129709.q: Which tax do companies pay to the cantons on their equity?
129709.e: Besides profit tax, legal persons pay a capital tax in the cantons. The Confederation no longer levies a capital tax.
129709.m: Companies pay capital tax in the cantons.

129710.q: Why are dividends from larger shareholdings in a company only partly taxed as income?
a: To ease the double burden on company profit and dividend
Because shareholders do not have to pay taxes
Because the bank keeps the tax
129710.e: The profit has already been taxed at company level. For holdings of 10 per cent or more, the dividend is therefore only partly taxed.
129710.m: Partial taxation eases the double burden.

129711.q: Mrs Bianchi sells a flat for more than she paid for it. Which tax is due on the profit?
129711.e: Profits from selling private shares are tax-free, profits from property are not. All cantons levy a property gains tax.

129712.q: What is the property transfer tax that some cantons levy?
a: A tax when a property changes owner
129712.e: When a property changes owner, some cantons charge a property transfer tax. Other cantons have abolished it.
129712.m: Property transfer tax: when a property changes owner.

129713.q: In some cantons, who can be taxed on expenditure instead of income?
a: All pensioners with an AHV pension
129713.e: With taxation on expenditure, also called lump-sum taxation, tax is based on living costs. It only applies to certain foreigners, not to Swiss citizens, and some cantons have abolished it.
129713.m: Taxation on expenditure only exists for certain foreigners.

129714.q: Which federal levy is due when trading securities through a securities dealer?
a: The securities transfer tax, a stamp duty
129714.e: The Confederation’s stamp duties include, among others, the transfer tax on buying and selling securities.
129714.m: A stamp duty is due when trading securities.

129715.q: What does a double taxation agreement between Switzerland and another country regulate?
a: Which state may tax which income
Which language applies on tax forms
That nobody pays taxes any more
129715.e: Agreements like this prevent people with ties to two countries from paying tax twice on the same income.
129715.m: Agreements prevent double taxation between countries.

129716.q: What happens with the automatic exchange of information (AEOI) on financial accounts?
a: Banks report accounts of people abroad to their country of residence
Banks publish all account balances online
The tax office swaps forms with Swiss Post
129716.e: With the AEOI, Swiss banks send account data of people resident in partner states to their tax authorities. This is meant to prevent cross-border tax evasion.
129716.m: With the AEOI, account data goes to the country of residence.

129717.q: What is the withholding tax mainly for, for people in Switzerland?
a: To make sure interest and dividends are declared honestly
129717.e: If you declare interest and dividends honestly, you get the withholding tax back. If you conceal them, you lose it. That is why it is called a safeguard tax.

129718.q: The tax office rejects Mrs Kälin’s objection. What can she do then?
a: Take the decision to a court
Send a new tax return with lower figures
129718.e: After the decision on the objection, you can appeal to a tax court. In the end the case can go as far as the Federal Supreme Court.
129718.m: After the objection comes the route to court.

129719.q: What does the duty to cooperate in tax proceedings mean?
a: You must give information and submit documents on request
You must work at the tax office
You must help others with their tax return
You must move house every year
129719.e: Taxpayers must do everything needed for the tax office to assess them correctly, for example submit documents.
129719.m: Taxpayers must provide information and documents.

129720.q: As a rule, for how long can the tax office tax concealed income afterwards?
a: Up to 10 years after the end of the tax period
129720.e: The right to start supplementary tax proceedings usually expires ten years after the end of the tax period concerned.
129720.m: Back taxes can be charged up to ten years back.

129721.q: A separated father pays maintenance for his underage child to the mother. What applies for tax?
a: He can deduct it, the mother pays tax on it
Both have to pay tax on it
The child has to pay tax on it
129721.e: The person paying maintenance for underage children may deduct it. The parent who receives it pays tax on it as income.
129721.m: Child maintenance: payer deducts, recipient pays tax.

129722.q: Both parents work and their child goes to a day nursery. What can they do in their tax return?
a: Deduct the nursery costs up to a maximum amount
The nursery has to fill in the tax return
The child is exempted from tax
129722.e: Costs for childcare by third parties can be deducted up to a maximum amount if they are needed because of work or training.
129722.m: Nursery costs can be deducted up to a maximum.

129723.q: For other work-related expenses, what can you usually choose?
a: A flat-rate deduction or the actual costs with receipts
Double your pay as a deduction
129723.e: There is a flat rate for other work-related expenses. If your costs are higher, you can prove the actual costs.
129723.m: Work expenses: flat rate or receipts.

129724.q: Mr Lüthi voluntarily pays extra money into his pension fund to close gaps. What applies for tax?
a: The buy-in can be deducted from income
He has to pay double tax on it
He gets the money back straight away
129724.e: Buy-ins to the pension fund are deductible. If capital is withdrawn within three years, the deduction can be lost.

129725.q: A self-employed graphic designer has no pension fund. What applies to her pillar 3a?
a: She may pay in and deduct a higher amount
She may not pay in at all
She may only pay in half the amount
She has to pay tax on the payment
129725.e: People who do not belong to a pension fund may pay a larger share of their income into pillar 3a, up to a maximum amount.
129725.m: Without a pension fund, a higher 3a limit applies.

129726.q: What may you withdraw money from pillar 3a for before retirement age?
a: For your own home that you live in
For a holiday in the Maldives
129726.e: An early withdrawal is only allowed in certain cases, for example for owner-occupied property, starting self-employment or emigrating for good.
129726.m: 3a money is only available early in certain cases.

129727.q: How is a pension from the pension fund generally taxed?
129727.e: Contributions to the pension fund could be deducted earlier. That is why the later pension is taxed as income.
129727.m: Pension fund pensions are taxable income.

a: On a pay-as-you-go basis: today’s contributions pay today’s pensions
Each person saves only for themselves in their own account
Only with interest from the National Bank
129728.e: In the AHV, a year’s income is used directly for that year’s pensions. That is why the ratio of workers to pensioners matters a lot.
129728.m: The AHV works on a pay-as-you-go basis.

129729.q: How does the financing of the pension fund work, unlike the AHV?
a: Each insured person builds up their own retirement capital
Today’s contributions directly pay today’s pensions
It is paid for only with taxes
It has no money at all
129729.e: In the 2nd pillar, a retirement balance is built up and invested for each person. This is called the funded system.
129729.m: The pension fund saves capital for each person.

129730.q: Where is the three-pillar principle of Swiss retirement provision laid down?
129730.e: The Federal Constitution describes the three pillars: state provision (AHV/IV), occupational provision and private provision.
129730.m: The three pillars are in the Federal Constitution.

129731.q: What happens if someone has not paid AHV contributions for some years?
a: The later AHV pension is reduced
Nothing, the pension is the same for everyone
129731.e: A full pension requires an unbroken record of contribution years. Each missing year reduces the pension.
129731.m: Contribution gaps reduce the AHV pension.

129732.q: Elena is studying and not working. From when does she still have to pay AHV contributions?
a: Never, as long as she is studying
From her first day at school
129732.e: Non-working people such as students also have to pay contributions from 1 January after their 20th birthday, otherwise gaps arise.
129732.m: Non-working people pay AHV from the January after their 20th birthday.

129733.q: What applies to self-employed people regarding unemployment insurance?
a: They are the only ones insured
129733.e: Unemployment insurance is meant for employees. Self-employed people pay no contributions and get no unemployment benefit when work dries up.
129733.m: The self-employed have no unemployment insurance.

129734.q: How are the supplementary benefits to the AHV and IV financed?
a: By the Confederation and cantons with tax money
129734.e: Supplementary benefits help when pension and assets are not enough for the subsistence minimum. They are paid from general tax revenue.
129734.m: Supplementary benefits come from tax money.

129735.q: Where does most of the levy that casinos in Switzerland pay on their gaming revenue go?
129735.e: The casino levy on gross gaming revenue mostly goes to the AHV.
129735.m: The casino levy helps the AHV.

129736.q: How is a large part of the CO2 levy on heating oil and gas redistributed to the population?
a: Equally via the health insurance premium
Not at all, the Confederation keeps it all
Only to owners of oil heating
129736.e: Every insured person receives the same amount via their health insurance premium bill. People who cause little CO2 benefit from this.
129736.m: The CO2 levy is redistributed via health insurance.

129737.q: What is the main aim of an incentive tax?
a: To influence a particular behaviour, not to raise money
To raise as much money as possible for the state
129737.e: An incentive tax makes something harmful more expensive so that less of it is used. The revenue is often redistributed.

129738.q: What do fees, preferential charges and exemption levies have in common?
a: They are causal charges with a specific reason for payment
They are only levied by the Confederation
129738.e: Causal charges are linked to a particular service, an advantage or an unfulfilled duty. Taxes, by contrast, are owed unconditionally.
129738.m: Causal charges have a specific reason.

129739.q: The municipality builds a road to a new housing area. The landowners have to pay a development contribution. What is this?
a: A preferential charge, because they have a particular advantage
129739.e: Anyone who gains a particular economic advantage from a public facility pays a contribution towards its costs. This is called a preferential charge.
129739.m: Those with a particular advantage pay a contribution.

129740.q: What does the cost-coverage principle for fees say?
a: Fees as a whole may not exceed the costs
Fees must bring the highest possible profit
129740.e: With fees the state is meant to cover its costs, but not make a profit.

129741.q: What does the equivalence principle require of a fee?
a: It must be in reasonable proportion to the value of the service
It must be the same for all services
It must be twice the costs
It may only be paid in francs
129741.e: A fee may not be obviously too high compared with what you get for it.

129742.q: What does it mean if a tax is earmarked?
a: Its revenue may only be used for a particular purpose
You may only pay it for a particular purpose
129742.e: With earmarking, it is fixed what the money is used for, for example part of the mineral oil tax for road traffic.
129742.m: Earmarked: the money has a fixed purpose.

129743.q: What does a country’s tax-to-GDP ratio show?
a: The share of taxes and social contributions in economic output
129743.e: The ratio compares all taxes and social insurance contributions with gross domestic product. This allows countries to be compared.
129743.m: The tax ratio measures a country’s tax burden.

129744.q: What is VAT accounting with the net tax rate method?
a: Simplified accounting for smaller firms with a fixed sector rate on turnover
A penalty for accounting too late
A discount for customers at the till
A rate that only applies to exports
129744.e: Instead of deducting input tax item by item, smaller firms can apply a net tax rate to turnover. It takes into account the typical input tax of the sector.
129744.m: The net tax rate simplifies VAT for small firms.

129745.q: What is a financial referendum, as many cantons have?
a: The people can vote on large new expenditure
A check of the tax return
A loan from the National Bank
129745.e: In many cantons and municipalities, spending above a certain limit goes to a popular vote. At federal level there is no financial referendum.
129745.m: In a financial referendum, the people decide on spending.

129746.q: Which rule has applied in Switzerland since 2024 to very large international groups?
a: They must pay at least 15 per cent profit tax
They no longer pay any taxes
They must pay 50 per cent profit tax
129746.e: With the minimum tax under OECD and G20 rules, groups with very high turnover are taxed at at least 15 per cent. If the tax is lower, a top-up tax is added.
129746.m: Large groups pay at least 15 per cent.

129747.q: A Swiss company sells machines to Germany. What applies for Swiss VAT?
a: Exports are exempt from Swiss VAT
The customer pays Swiss VAT twice
The company pays a penalty tax
The machines are taxed at the standard rate
129747.e: VAT is meant to be charged where things are consumed. Exports are exempt, and the company can still deduct input tax.

129748.q: For which service is no VAT charged in Switzerland because it is excluded?
129748.e: Medical treatments in healthcare are excluded from VAT, as are, for example, school lessons and flat rents.
129748.m: Medical treatment is excluded from VAT.

129749.q: Suppose the VAT rate were 10 per cent. A baker buys flour for 100 francs and sells bread made from it for 300 francs (excluding VAT). How much VAT does he pass on after deducting input tax?
129749.e: On the sale he owes 30 francs, and he paid 10 francs of input tax on the flour. 30 minus 10 makes 20 francs, so 10 per cent of his added value of 200 francs.
129749.m: What is passed on is the VAT on the added value.

129750.q: Why does VAT weigh relatively more heavily on people with a low income?
a: They spend a larger share of their income on consumption
They pay a higher VAT rate
They have to pay VAT twice
They do not get till receipts
129750.e: People who earn little can hardly save and spend almost everything. That is why VAT makes up a bigger share of their income. The lower rate for food eases this.
129750.m: VAT hits small incomes proportionally harder.

129751.q: The Confederation’s profit tax for companies is proportional. What does that mean?
a: The same percentage applies to every profit
The rate rises with the profit
Small companies pay a higher percentage than large ones
The tax is the same number of francs for all companies
129751.e: With a proportional tax the percentage stays the same. A profit twice as high results in a tax twice as high.
129751.m: Proportional means always the same percentage.

129752.q: Suppose the first 20,000 francs are tax-free and 10 per cent applies to every franc above that. How much tax do you pay on a taxable income of 50,000 francs?
129752.e: Only the 30,000 francs above the tax-free amount are taxed. 10 per cent of that is 3000 francs.
129752.m: First subtract the tax-free amount, then apply the rate.

129753.q: Someone with a taxable income of 50,000 francs pays 3000 francs in tax. What is their average tax rate?
129753.e: 3000 divided by 50,000 makes 0.06, so 6 per cent. The marginal tax rate can be higher.
129753.m: Average rate equals tax divided by income.

129754.q: A deduction lowers taxable income by 1000 francs. The marginal tax rate is 30 per cent. Roughly how much tax do you save?
129754.e: A deduction does not save its whole amount, only the tax on it: 30 per cent of 1000 francs is 300 francs.
129754.m: A deduction saves the amount times the marginal tax rate.

129755.q: Sara gets 2000 francs more pay a year. Her marginal tax rate is 25 per cent. Roughly how much of it does she keep after tax?
129755.e: On the extra 2000 francs she pays 25 per cent, so 500 francs in tax. 1500 francs are left. So a pay rise is always worth it.
129755.m: Despite progression, more pay brings more money.

129756.q: How are taxing powers basically divided between the Confederation and the cantons?
a: Cantons may levy all taxes that the Constitution does not reserve for the Confederation
Only the Confederation may levy taxes
Cantons need permission from the municipalities for every tax
The Confederation may levy any tax it likes without the Constitution
129756.e: The Confederation may only levy taxes that the Federal Constitution expressly allows. Otherwise the cantons are free, but must respect the harmonisation law.
129756.m: The Confederation needs a constitutional basis for every tax.

129757.q: What is equalised in the resource equalisation part of fiscal equalisation between the cantons?
a: Differences in the cantons’ financial capacity
Differences in the number of mountains
The size of the cantonal flags
129757.e: Cantons with high tax potential and the Confederation give money to cantons with low tax potential. That way all of them should be able to carry out their tasks.

129758.q: A mountain canton has high costs for roads and protective structures because of its location. How does the Confederation’s fiscal equalisation help?
a: With cost equalisation for special burdens
Not at all, it has to bear them alone
It may levy its own VAT
The neighbouring cantons have to build the roads
129758.e: As well as resource equalisation, there is cost equalisation for cantons with special burdens due to their topography or population structure.
129758.m: Cost equalisation helps with special costs.

129759.q: Is there also fiscal equalisation between the municipalities of a canton?
a: Yes, the cantons have their own equalisation systems for their municipalities
Only between municipalities in different countries
129759.e: The cantons balance out large differences between financially strong and weak municipalities. The rules vary from canton to canton.

a: People who work for the tax authorities may not pass on tax data
You may not show your own tax return to anyone
The tax office does not reveal how many taxes there are
Tax forms are secret army documents
129760.e: Staff of the tax authorities are bound by confidentiality. They may only pass on what the law expressly allows.
129760.m: Tax data is protected by tax secrecy.

129761.q: What do many cantons pay if you pay your taxes before the due date?
129761.e: If you pay early, you are in a way lending the canton money. In many cantons you get a small amount of interest for this.

129762.q: Lukas’s employer refunds his train ticket for a business trip. Is this taxable income?
a: No, expenses only replace costs incurred for work
Only if he travels first class
129762.e: Expenses that replace actual work costs are not income. Flat-rate expenses, however, must appear on the salary statement.
129762.m: Genuine expense refunds are not income.

129763.q: An employee on a farm gets free board and lodging as well as her pay in money. What applies for tax?
a: Board and lodging count as income in kind
They are tax-free because no money changes hands
The farmer has to declare them as a donation
They only count for the dog tax
129763.e: Benefits that are not paid in money are also income. Board and lodging are valued at fixed rates.
129763.m: Income in kind is income too.

129764.q: Mr Kunz may also use his company car privately. What applies for tax?
a: The value of the private use counts as income
Only the employer pays dog tax for it
He may deduct the car from his income
129764.e: Private use is a benefit with monetary value. It is usually calculated at a flat rate and shown on the salary statement.
129764.m: Private use of a company car is income.

129765.q: Military pay is tax-free. What applies to the income compensation (EO) during service?
a: It has to be paid back
129765.e: The EO replaces pay and is therefore taxed like pay. Only the military pay itself is tax-free.
129765.m: Replacement pay is taxable like pay.

129766.q: After losing her job, Nadine receives daily allowances from unemployment insurance. What applies for tax?
a: The daily allowances are taxable income
They are deducted from her assets
They only count for church tax
129766.e: Daily allowances replace pay and are therefore taxable. The unemployment fund issues a certificate for the tax return.

129767.q: What applies to social assistance payments for income tax?
a: They must be declared as profit
129767.e: Support from public funds such as social assistance is exempt from income tax.

129768.q: Jana sells her old bike privately for 300 francs. Does she have to pay income tax on the proceeds?
a: No, private capital gains on movable assets are tax-free
Yes, always on the full amount
Only if the buyer lives abroad
129768.e: Selling private items such as a bike is not taxable income, as long as it is not trading as an occupation.
129768.m: Selling private items is usually tax-free.

129769.q: Tim owns bitcoin. What applies to it in his tax return?
a: He must declare it as assets at the year-end price
You never have to declare cryptocurrencies
He must declare it as wages
Only the purchase has to be reported
129769.e: Cryptocurrencies are part of your assets. The Federal Tax Administration publishes prices for them as of 31 December.
129769.m: Crypto belongs in the list of securities.

129770.q: In many cantons, what applies to church tax for companies?
a: Legal persons have to pay church tax too
Companies pay their employees’ church tax
Companies are always members of a church
129770.e: In many cantons companies also pay church taxes, even though they cannot leave the Church. Some cantons do not have this.
129770.m: In many cantons companies pay church tax.

129771.q: Parliament passes a new federal tax law. How can the people have it put to a vote?
a: With 50,000 signatures within 100 days for a referendum
With a letter to the tax office
Not at all, laws are final
129771.e: An optional referendum can be called against federal laws. This requires 50,000 valid signatures within 100 days.

129772.q: A municipality wants to have a school building built. What does it usually have to do for large contracts?
a: Put the contract out to public tender
Always give the contract to the mayor’s company
Have the schoolchildren do the work
129772.e: Above certain thresholds, public contracts must be put out to tender. That way tax money is meant to be used economically and fairly.
129772.m: Large public contracts are put out to tender.

129773.q: How long is it sensible to keep tax documents and important receipts?
129773.e: Because the tax office can claim back taxes up to ten years later, it is advisable to keep documents that long.
129773.m: Keep tax documents for about ten years.

129774.q: Which two taxes bring the Confederation the most money?
a: The dog tax and the tourist tax
The beer tax and the ticket tax
The motorway sticker and the boat tax
129774.e: Together, VAT and direct federal tax make up most of the Confederation’s income.
129774.m: VAT and federal tax are the main federal income.

129775.q: At minimum, how much must an employer pay towards its employees’ pension fund contributions?
a: At least as much as the employees together
129775.e: The law requires the employer to bear at least half of the contributions. Many employers pay more.
129775.m: The employer pays at least half the pension fund contributions.

129776.q: Who pays the premium for the compulsory insurance against occupational accidents?
129776.e: The employer bears the premium for occupational accidents. The premium for non-occupational accidents may be deducted from the employees’ pay.
129776.m: The employer insures occupational accidents at its own cost.

129777.q: Who orders regional passenger transport by bus and train and covers the costs not covered by fares?
129777.e: The Confederation and cantons order routes from transport companies and cover the costs not met by tickets.
129777.m: The Confederation and cantons order regional transport.

129778.q: Maria moves abroad for good in June. What applies to her Swiss income tax?
a: Her tax liability ends when she leaves, and she is taxed until then
She pays double for the whole year
She never pays taxes again, not even for January to June
She must still submit a Swiss tax return every year
129778.e: On leaving, unlimited tax liability ends. She still has to pay taxes for the months until she leaves and deregister.
129778.m: Tax liability ends when you move away.

129779.q: Paul moves to Switzerland from abroad in July. How is his tax rate for this year worked out?
a: For the rate, his income is extrapolated to twelve months
He pays no taxes for half years
He automatically pays the highest rate
He pays the rate of his former country
129779.e: Only the income from his arrival is taxed. So that the rate is fair, it is converted to a whole year to determine the rate.
129779.m: On arrival, the extrapolated annual income counts for the rate.

129780.q: A person lives in Germany and owns a holiday flat in Valais. What applies in Switzerland?
a: They have limited tax liability in Switzerland for the holiday flat
They have to pay Swiss tax on their entire income
They pay nothing at all in Switzerland
They have to move to Switzerland
129780.e: Anyone who owns property in Switzerland is liable to tax on it here, even without living here. This is called economic allegiance.
129780.m: Property is taxed where it is located.

129781.q: Which value applies to listed shares in the tax return?
a: The price on 31 December according to the tax administration’s price list
The purchase price from ten years ago
The highest price of the year
129781.e: The Federal Tax Administration publishes a price list with tax values at the end of the year. These values apply for wealth tax.
129781.m: Shares count at the year-end price.

129782.q: Lara has an account in euros. How does she declare the balance in her tax return?
a: Converted into francs at the rate on 31 December
Not at all, foreign currencies do not count
At the rate on the day the account was opened
129782.e: All values are stated in francs. For foreign currencies, the exchange rates at the end of the year apply.
129782.m: Convert foreign currencies into francs at year end.

129783.q: A young company makes losses in its first years and a profit later. What does tax law allow?
a: Offsetting losses from the last seven years against later profits
Deducting the losses as a donation
Charging the losses to the founders
Nothing at all, losses never count
129783.e: Companies may deduct losses from the seven previous business years from later profits.
129783.m: Company losses can be carried forward for seven years.

129784.q: In Switzerland, how are the taxes a company pays treated when calculating its taxable profit?
a: They count as a business-related expense
They are added to the profit
They may not be paid at all
129784.e: Unlike in many countries, profit and capital taxes in Switzerland are deductible as an expense. As a result the statutory rate is higher than the effective burden.
129784.m: Company taxes are a deductible expense in Switzerland.

129785.q: What was the company tax reform (STAF), approved by the people in 2019, linked to?
129785.e: The bill abolished special rules for certain companies and at the same time brought extra money for the AHV every year.
129785.m: The STAF linked tax reform and AHV funding.

129786.q: May a canton introduce its own additional VAT?
a: No, VAT is reserved for the Confederation
Yes, every canton as it likes
129786.e: The Federal Constitution forbids the cantons to levy taxes that the Confederation levies as VAT.
129786.m: VAT is purely a federal matter.

129787.q: Do you have to pay income tax on an inheritance?
a: No, at most there is the cantonal inheritance tax
Yes, at double the federal rate
129787.e: Inheritances are exempt from income tax. Depending on the canton and degree of kinship, an inheritance tax is due. The inherited assets then count as part of your assets.

129788.q: A foreign online shop sells many small consignments to Switzerland. What applies above a certain annual turnover?
a: It must register for VAT in Switzerland
It is exempt from VAT for ever
Swiss Post pays the VAT for it
129788.e: Since 2019, foreign mail-order sellers above a certain turnover from small consignments must account for VAT in Switzerland. That way Swiss sellers are not disadvantaged.
129788.m: Large foreign online shops pay Swiss VAT.

129789.q: Which department does the Federal Tax Administration belong to?
129789.e: The Federal Department of Finance is responsible for the Confederation’s finances. The tax administration is part of it.
129789.m: The tax administration belongs to the Department of Finance.

129790.q: When the Swiss National Bank distributes a profit, how is it divided?
a: One third to the Confederation, two thirds to the cantons
129790.e: The Federal Constitution states that at least two thirds of the net profit go to the cantons. Distributions only happen if the National Bank’s situation allows.
129790.m: Two thirds of National Bank profits go to the cantons.

129791.q: When can gains from selling shares be taxed for a private individual after all?
a: If they count as a professional securities dealer
If the shares come from Switzerland
If the gain is under 100 francs
129791.e: Anyone who trades very often, with large sums or on credit can count as professional. Then the gains are income from self-employment.

129792.q: The Steiner family rents out a room in their flat to tourists through a platform. What applies for tax?
a: The rental income is taxable income
The money is tax-free because it is private
Only the tourists have to pay taxes
Only the platform has to declare it
129792.e: Rental income is income and belongs in the tax return. Depending on the place, tourist tax must also be accounted for.
129792.m: You must pay tax on rental income.

129793.q: Lena regularly sells home-made jewellery online and earns money from it. What applies?
a: The profit is taxable and AHV contributions may be due
She only has to pay VAT on every franc
129793.e: A regular activity aimed at making a profit is self-employment. The profit is taxed and AHV contributions may be owed.
129793.m: An online side income is income.

129794.q: An influencer gets products free from companies in return for promotional posts. What applies for tax?
a: The value of the products counts as income
The followers have to pay the taxes
129794.e: Anyone who receives goods as payment for a service has income in kind. It must be declared at market value.

129795.q: What does it mean if a municipality has a high tax capacity?
a: It takes in a lot of tax per resident
It has particularly strong tax officials
It has the highest tax multiplier
It pays no taxes to the canton
129795.e: Tax capacity shows how much tax a municipality would take in per head at a uniform tax multiplier. Municipalities with high tax capacity often pay into fiscal equalisation.
129795.m: High tax capacity means a lot of tax per head.

129796.q: A student from the canton of Uri studies at the University of Zurich. Who pays the university a contribution towards his education?
a: The municipality where the university is
129796.e: Under an intercantonal agreement, the home cantons pay contributions to universities in other cantons where their students study.
129796.m: The home canton contributes to the studies.

129797.q: For direct federal tax, what applies to the deduction for travel costs to work?
a: It is limited to a maximum amount
129797.e: Since the railway infrastructure bill, the travel cost deduction at federal level has been capped. Many cantons also have an upper limit.
129797.m: Travel costs are only deductible up to a limit.

129798.q: What applies to child and education allowances for income tax?
a: The child has to pay tax on them
129798.e: Family allowances are part of the parents’ income. They usually appear on the salary statement and are taxed with the pay.

129799.q: Mr Graf dies and still has unpaid tax debts. What applies to his heirs?
a: They are liable for the tax debts, at most up to their share of the inheritance
The municipality pays them from its budget
Only the notary has to pay them
129799.e: Anyone who inherits also takes on the debts, including unpaid taxes. For taxes, liability is limited to the share of the inheritance.
129799.m: Heirs also take on unpaid taxes.

129800.q: Where is a public limited company in Switzerland basically taxed?
a: At its registered office or place of actual management
In the canton with the lowest tax multiplier, freely chosen without an office
129800.e: Legal persons have unlimited tax liability where their registered office or actual management is. For permanent establishments in other cantons, the tax is divided up.
129800.m: Companies pay tax at their registered office.

129801.q: A club pursues exclusively charitable purposes and is recognised by the canton. What applies to its profit tax?
a: It can be exempted from profit and capital tax
It has to tax its members
129801.e: Organisations that pursue exclusively charitable purposes can be exempted from tax. That is why donations to them are deductible.

129802.q: Which people in Switzerland are largely exempt from direct taxes under international agreements?
129802.e: Under the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, diplomats are largely exempt from direct taxes in the host country.
129802.m: Diplomats are largely exempt from direct taxes.

129803.q: Tom accidentally kicks the ball through the neighbour's window. The glass breaks. Which insurance helps the family?
129803.e: Liability insurance pays for damage you accidentally cause to other people. The broken window belongs to the neighbour.
129803.m: Liability insurance pays for damage you cause to others.

a: For damage you cause to others
129804.e: If you break something that belongs to another person, you have to pay for the damage. Liability insurance covers that.
129804.m: Liability insurance helps when you break something of someone else's.

129805.q: What does household contents insurance cover?
a: Your own things in the flat
129805.e: Household contents include furniture, clothes, toys, books and appliances. Contents insurance helps if they are damaged by fire, water or a break-in, for example.
129805.m: Household contents are your own things in the flat.

129806.q: The Keller family's washing machine leaks. Their own carpet is soaked and ruined. Which insurance helps?
129806.e: The carpet belongs to the family itself. Water damage to your own things is paid by household contents insurance.
129806.m: Own things damaged by water: contents insurance.

129807.q: The Graf family's flat has been broken into. Who does the family call first?
129807.e: After a break-in you first call the police on 117. Then you report the damage to the household contents insurance.
129807.m: After a break-in, call the police first.

129808.q: What does an insurance company call a “claim” or damage?
a: When something is broken or lost
129808.e: Damage could be a broken window, a soaked sofa or a stolen bike, for example. Then insurance can help.
129808.m: Damage means something is broken or gone.

129809.q: What do you usually get from the insurance when insured damage happens?
129809.e: The insurance pays for the repair or for something new as a replacement. In return you pay the premium regularly beforehand.
129809.m: Insurance pays for repair or replacement.

129810.q: Lina has a sore throat. Where can her mum get throat lozenges without a prescription and good advice?
129810.e: At the pharmacy many medicines are available without a prescription. The staff there give advice on what helps.
129810.m: The pharmacy gives advice even without a prescription.

129811.q: What does the date on a medicine pack show?
a: Until when you may use the medicine
When the doctor is on holiday
129811.e: After the expiry date a medicine may no longer work properly. Then you should not take it any more.
129811.m: You do not take expired medicines.

129812.q: What do you do with old medicines you no longer need?
a: Take them back to the pharmacy
129812.e: Medicines do not belong in the toilet or in nature. The pharmacy takes them back and disposes of them properly.
129812.m: Take old medicines back to the pharmacy.

129813.q: What is the leaflet in a medicine pack called that says how to take the medicine?
129813.e: The package leaflet says what the medicine is for, how much to take and what to watch out for. Adults read it carefully.
129813.m: The package leaflet explains the medicine.

129814.q: The pharmacist asks how old Noah is. Why does she want to know?
a: The amount of medicine depends on age
She wants to give him a present
She is writing a birthday card
She needs it for a game
129814.e: Children often need less of a medicine than adults. That is why the pharmacy asks about age and sometimes weight.
129814.m: Children often need a smaller amount.

a: A pharmacy that also helps at night or on Sundays
129815.e: When the other pharmacies are closed, an emergency pharmacy is on duty. So you can get important medicines even in the evening or on a Sunday.
129815.m: The emergency pharmacy helps at night and on Sundays too.

129816.q: Which number can children and young people call if they are worried and want to talk to someone?
129816.e: On 147, experts from Pro Juventute advise children and young people, free and in confidence. You can also chat or write.

129817.e: In an emergency someone is in danger, for example badly injured or unconscious. Then you get help at once.
129817.m: In an emergency you get help immediately.

129818.q: On the tram a woman suddenly faints. What do you do first as a child?
a: Call loudly to an adult for help
129818.e: Children can help very well by calling adults. The adults can then dial the emergency number 144.
129818.m: Getting help is already first aid.

129819.q: What is the health insurance called that is compulsory for everyone in Switzerland?
129819.e: Everyone who lives in Switzerland must have basic insurance. It helps when you are ill and pays for the doctor and hospital, for example.
129819.m: Basic insurance is compulsory for everyone.

129820.e: You can choose to add supplementary insurance to basic insurance. It pays for things that basic insurance does not cover.

129821.q: What is written on every bill?
a: How much you have to pay
What the weather will be like
129821.e: A bill says what you have to pay for and how much. It often also says by when you should pay.
129821.m: The bill says how much you have to pay.

129822.q: A bill says “payable within 30 days”. What does that mean?
a: You are not allowed to pay for 30 days
129822.e: The payment deadline says by when the money should be paid. If you pay late, you often get a reminder.
129822.m: The deadline says by when you pay.

129823.q: What is a receipt for after you have paid?
a: It proves that you have paid
129823.e: A receipt shows that something has already been paid. You keep important receipts, for the insurance for example.

129824.q: What do you often get if you pay a bill too late?
129824.e: If you do not pay a bill on time, a reminder arrives. It reminds you that the money is still owed.
129824.m: A reminder is about an unpaid bill.

129825.q: What protects you best from injuries when inline skating?
a: A helmet and knee and wrist guards
129825.e: When inline skating you often fall on your hands and knees. A helmet and guards protect your head and joints.
129825.m: Skating is safer with a helmet and guards.

a: Lena trips and breaks her foot
129826.e: An accident happens suddenly from outside, for example a fall. A cold, a sore throat and a temperature are illnesses.
129826.m: A fall is an accident, flu is an illness.

129827.q: Which example is an illness and not an accident?
a: A broken arm after a fall
A bump from falling off a bike
129827.e: Flu comes from viruses in the body. The other examples are injuries from outside, so they are accidents.

129828.q: Lio rides his scooter into a parked car and makes a scratch. Who usually pays for the damage?
129828.e: The car belongs to someone else. Damage to others is paid by liability insurance, which often covers the whole family.
129828.m: Scratch on someone else's car: liability insurance.

129829.q: You accidentally break your friend's toy. What is the right thing to do?
a: Say so honestly and tell your parents
129829.e: If you report damage honestly, it can be sorted out. Your parents know whether an insurance can help.

129830.q: Oil is burning in a pan. What is the best way to smother the fire?
129830.e: Water on burning oil is very dangerous: it spatters and the fire gets bigger. A lid cuts off the fire's air.
129830.m: Never put water on burning oil!

129831.q: What does a smoke alarm in the flat do?
a: It beeps loudly when there is smoke
It plays music in the morning
129831.e: A smoke alarm gives an early warning if there is a fire. So you can quickly leave the flat and call the fire brigade.
129831.m: The smoke alarm warns you of smoke.

129832.q: You do not know how much of a syrup you are allowed to take. What do you do?
a: Ask at the pharmacy or the doctor
129832.e: With medicines the right amount is important. The pharmacy and the doctor know exactly.

129833.q: Where should the emergency numbers be written at home?
a: Clearly visible, on the fridge for example
In a box in the cellar
129833.e: In an emergency things must happen fast. If the numbers are clearly visible, everyone finds them at once.
129833.m: Emergency numbers hang where they can be seen.

129834.q: Who pays the health insurance premium when you are grown up and earn your own money?
129834.e: For children it is usually the parents who pay. Adults normally pay their own premium.
129834.m: Adults usually pay their own premium.

129835.q: What helps against tick bites in the woods?
a: Long trousers and checking your body afterwards
129835.e: Ticks often sit in grass and bushes. Long clothes protect you, and after the woods you check your body.
129835.m: After the woods, check your body for ticks.

129836.q: What protects you best from sunburn?
a: Sun cream, a hat and shade at midday
Lying in the midday sun for a long time
129836.e: The sun is strongest at midday. Shade, clothes, a hat and sun cream protect your skin.
129836.m: At midday, stay in the shade.

129837.q: What is the rule for small children near water?
a: They may go into deep water alone
It is best if they jump off the diving board alone
129837.e: Small children can drown quickly and silently. That is why an adult always stays very close.
129837.m: Never leave small children alone near water.

129838.q: What protects your head when skiing and snowboarding?
129838.e: In a fall on the slope your head can hit hard. A ski helmet protects it.
129838.m: On the slopes you wear a helmet.

129839.q: The Meier family's dog tears a neighbour child's jacket. Which insurance pays for the jacket?
129839.e: If you own a dog, you are responsible for damage it causes. Liability insurance covers that.
129839.m: Damage caused by your own dog: liability insurance.

129840.q: What does an insurance company do with the premiums of all the insured people?
a: It uses them to pay for the damage
It hands the money out at the end of the year
129840.e: Many people pay premiums, and from these the insurance pays the few who have damage. So nobody has to bear everything alone.
129840.m: Damage is paid out of everyone's premiums.

129841.q: Jan's new bike is stolen outside the school. What helps make this happen less often?
a: Always locking the bike with a good lock
Leaving the key in the lock
Leaving the bike unlocked on the street
129841.e: A locked bike is stolen far less often. Some insurers also only pay if the bike was locked.

129842.q: What happens in hospital before you are allowed to go home?
a: The doctor says you are well enough
You have to sit an exam
You have to buy the bed yourself
You have to sing a song
129842.e: The doctors decide when you can go home. You often get some tips or medicines to take with you.
129842.m: The doctor says when you can go home.

129843.q: What do you take to the doctor's surgery so you are not bored while waiting?
a: A football to play with in the waiting room
A loud music player without headphones
129843.e: Other ill people are sitting in the waiting room too. A book is quiet and helps pass the time.
129843.m: You keep quiet in the waiting room.

129844.q: Who takes a small child's temperature?
a: The child all alone with a glass
Nobody, you never take a temperature
129844.e: Taking a temperature is easy, but with small children the parents help. Then they also know whether to go to the doctor.
129844.m: Adults help with taking a temperature.

129845.q: Sara reacts badly to peanuts. What is important?
a: Everyone who looks after her knows about it
She tries a little every day
129845.e: A strong allergy can become dangerous. Parents, teachers and carers must know about it.
129845.m: Tell all carers about a strong allergy.

129846.q: Why do you have insurance even though you hope nothing will happen?
a: So you do not have to pay alone if bad luck strikes
Because then you never get ill
Because you get money without anything happening
129846.e: Nobody knows whether an accident or damage will happen. The insurance helps if it does.
129846.m: Insurance helps when bad luck strikes.

129847.q: What belongs in a small first aid bag for a day trip?
129847.e: On a trip you can easily hurt yourself. With plasters and disinfectant you can treat small wounds.

129848.q: Ben has a small wood splinter in his finger. Who helps him get it out?
129848.e: A small splinter can be removed with clean tweezers. Afterwards you clean the spot.

129849.q: Ten children each put 2 francs into a kitty. How much money is in it?
129849.e: 10 times 2 francs is 20 francs. Insurance works the same way: many pay a little, and together it adds up to a lot.
129849.m: Many small amounts add up to a lot.

129850.q: Who may decide in Switzerland which health insurer a family is insured with?
129850.e: You can choose your health insurer yourself. There are many health insurers in Switzerland.
129850.m: You choose your health insurer yourself.

129851.q: A tooth breaks in a fall and the piece is lying on the ground. What do you do with the piece?
a: Pick it up and take it to the dentist
129851.e: Sometimes the dentist can stick the piece back on. It is best to bring it quickly and keep it moist, in milk for example.
129851.m: Take a broken piece of tooth with you.

129852.q: How does a bike helmet sit correctly?
a: Straight on the forehead and fastened tightly
At the back on the neck
129852.e: The helmet only protects you if it sits straight and the strap is fastened. It must not wobble.
129852.m: Put the helmet on straight and fasten it.

129853.q: The Rossi family is moving house. What do they take with them that counts as household contents?
129853.e: Household contents are the movable things you take with you when you move. Walls, windows and stairs are part of the building.
129853.m: You take your household contents when you move.

129854.q: Does health insurance cost the same for a child as for an adult?
a: No, it is cheaper for children
No, it is more expensive for children
129854.e: The health insurance premium is lower for children than for adults. That helps families.

129855.q: There is a fire in the flat, and your own clothes and bed are destroyed. Which insurance pays for the things?
129855.e: Household contents insurance pays for your own things destroyed by fire. Health insurance is for illness.
129855.m: Own things after a fire: contents insurance.

129856.q: What belongs to a family's household contents?
a: The road in front of the house
129856.e: Household contents are all the movable things in the flat. The walls and the roof are part of the building.
129856.m: Household contents are everything you take when you move.

129857.q: A heavy hailstorm damages the roof and windows of a house. Which insurance covers the house itself?
129857.e: The house itself is insured by buildings insurance. The things in the flat are insured by household contents insurance.

129858.q: What is the document called that says what a family has insured?
129858.e: The insurance policy says what is insured and how much it costs. You keep it in a safe place.
129858.m: The policy says what is insured.

129859.q: What does the doctor write on a prescription?
129859.e: You take the prescription to the pharmacy. There you get the medicine the doctor wrote down.
129859.m: You collect the medicine with the prescription.

129860.q: Why must you not eat medicines like sweets?
a: Too much can harm your body
Because they are only for animals
129860.e: Medicines only help in the right amount. Too much can be dangerous, even if they taste sweet.
129860.m: Medicines only in the right amount.

129861.q: What do you say on an emergency call so that help can find the way?
129861.e: The rescuers need to know where to go. That is why the address is very important.
129861.m: On an emergency call, always say where you are.

129862.q: Apart from your name and the place, what do you tell the emergency line?
129862.e: The person on the phone needs to know what has happened. Then they send the right help.
129862.m: On an emergency call, say what happened.

129863.q: What is the vehicle called that quickly takes injured people to hospital?
129863.e: An ambulance has medical equipment on board and drives with blue flashing lights.
129863.m: The ambulance takes injured people to hospital.

129864.q: Why is it best to keep medicines in their original pack?
a: So you know what it is and how to take it
129864.e: The pack shows the name, the expiry date and the leaflet with the instructions. Without the pack you could mix medicines up.
129864.m: Medicines stay in their original pack.

129865.q: When does the family pay the health insurance premium?
129865.e: You pay the premium regularly, even when everyone is healthy. Usually you pay every month.

129866.q: Who in Switzerland needs basic health insurance?
129866.e: Basic insurance is compulsory for everyone who lives in Switzerland, from babies to grandmothers.
129866.m: Everyone who lives here is insured.

129867.q: Basic insurance usually does not pay for a brace on your teeth. So what do many parents do early on?
129867.e: A brace can be expensive. It is best to take out supplementary dental insurance while the child is still small.
129867.m: Supplementary insurance helps with a brace.

a: A building where ill and injured people are treated
129868.e: Doctors, nurses and many others work in a hospital. They help ill and injured people, even at night.
129868.m: Ill people are treated in hospital.

129869.q: A child has had a mild cough for two days. Where does the family go if it does not get better?
a: To the paediatrician or family doctor
129869.e: For illnesses that are not dangerous you first go to the doctor's surgery. A&E is for serious cases.
129869.m: For a mild cough, go to the surgery first.

129870.q: When do you go to A&E (the emergency department) at the hospital?
a: With a serious injury or illness
129870.e: A&E is for people who need help immediately. Minor complaints are treated by the family doctor.

129871.q: What do you do with your insurance card so it does not get lost?
a: Always keep it in the same place
129871.e: You need the card at the doctor's and at the pharmacy. In the same place, your purse for example, you find it quickly.
129871.m: Your insurance card has a fixed place.

129872.q: What helps you get ill less often and cause fewer costs?
a: Eating healthily, moving and sleeping well
129872.e: A healthy daily life strengthens the body. Anyone who is ill less often needs fewer treatments.
129872.m: Living healthily also saves doctor's costs.

129873.q: Mila falls off the climbing frame at the playground. Her arm hurts badly. What do her parents do?
a: Do nothing and wait until tomorrow
129873.e: Severe pain after a fall can mean a broken bone. A doctor must look at the arm.
129873.m: Pain after a fall: go to the doctor.

129874.q: Who pays when a child on a visit accidentally knocks over the hosts' vase?
129874.e: The vase belongs to the hosts, so to someone else. That is what the child's family's liability insurance is for.
129874.m: Other people's things broken: liability insurance.

129875.q: Nina drops her own mobile phone and the screen breaks. Does her liability insurance pay?
a: No, it only pays for damage to others
Yes, if the phone is blue
129875.e: Liability insurance is for damage you cause to other people. It does not pay for your own things.
129875.m: Liability insurance does not pay for your own things.

129876.q: What do you do before putting a plaster on a friend's wound?
129876.e: With clean hands fewer germs get into the wound. Then you clean the wound and stick on the plaster.
129876.m: Wash your hands before treating a wound.

129877.q: A person is lying on the ground and does not respond. Which number do you call?
129877.e: If someone does not respond, it is an emergency. On 144 the ambulance service comes.
129877.m: Someone does not respond: call 144 at once.

129878.q: How should you speak on the emergency phone?
129878.e: The person on the phone must understand everything. Speaking calmly and clearly helps, even if you are scared.
129878.m: Speak calmly and clearly on an emergency call.

129879.q: Why is a stay in hospital expensive?
a: Many experts and machines help there
Because the bed is made of gold
129879.e: Many people work in a hospital day and night, and there are expensive machines. That is why health insurance helps to pay.
129879.m: Hospital is expensive, health insurance helps.

129880.q: The Huber family is flying off on holiday. What do the parents take for everyone in case someone gets ill?
129880.e: The back of the insurance card is often the European Health Insurance Card. It helps at the doctor's in many European countries.
129880.m: Take the insurance cards on holiday.

129881.q: What can the pharmacist do for minor complaints?
a: Give advice and a suitable remedy
129881.e: At the pharmacy you get advice for minor complaints like a runny nose. For serious problems the pharmacist sends you to the doctor.
129881.m: The pharmacy advises on minor complaints.

129882.q: What do you put on a larger wound that is bleeding?
129882.e: A clean bandage and gentle pressure stop the bleeding. With heavy bleeding you call 144.

129883.q: Why do some families photograph their valuable things at home?
a: So they can show what they had after damage
129883.e: After a fire or a break-in the insurance wants to know what is broken or missing. Photos and receipts help with that.

129884.q: Who can help you at school if you have hurt yourself?
129884.e: Teachers know about first aid and call the parents or the emergency number if needed.

129885.q: A child is ill and cannot go to school. What do the parents do?
129885.e: The school needs to know why a child is absent. The parents report the child as absent.
129885.m: If ill, the child is reported absent at school.

129886.e: In an operation many experts work with expensive equipment. That is why health insurance is especially important.

129887.q: What do you do if you have fallen off your bike and your head hurts?
a: Tell an adult and get checked
Throw the helmet away and say nothing
Shake your head until it stops
129887.e: A headache after a fall can be serious. An adult decides whether you need to see a doctor.
129887.m: Always report a headache after a fall.

129888.q: Leo rides his bike into a pedestrian's shopping trolley. The trolley is broken. Which insurance helps?
129888.e: The damage happened to another person. That is why the liability insurance of Leo's family pays.
129888.m: When cycling, liability insurance covers damage to others.

a: When someone takes something that is not theirs
When you borrow something and give it back
129889.e: A thief takes other people's things without asking. That is forbidden, and you report it to the police.

129890.q: In the medicine cabinet Mum finds an ointment that expired two years ago. What does she do?
a: She takes the ointment to the pharmacy
She gives it to the baby
She throws it in the stream
129890.e: Expired medicines may no longer work well. At the pharmacy they are disposed of properly.
129890.m: Expired items go back to the pharmacy.

129891.q: After the visit to the paediatrician a bill arrives. Who usually looks at it?
129891.e: The parents check the bill and see what the health insurance pays. Children can look too and learn from it.
129891.m: The parents check the doctor's bill.

129892.q: What do you take to a friend who is in hospital?
129892.e: Everyone in hospital needs rest. A card or a book brings joy and disturbs nobody.

129893.q: Which insurance pays when a child is ill and needs medicine from the doctor?
129893.e: Health insurance is responsible for illness. It helps pay for medicines prescribed by a doctor.
129893.m: When you are ill, health insurance helps.

a: There are different kinds for different damage
One single policy always pays for everything
129894.e: Health insurance helps with illness, contents insurance with your own things and liability insurance with damage to others.
129894.m: Each insurance has a different job.

129895.q: What is good for your body when you have a temperature?
a: A cold shower and going outside
129895.e: With a temperature your body is fighting an illness. Rest and lots of fluids help it.
129895.m: With a temperature: rest and drink.

129896.q: An elderly man has slipped on the pavement and cannot get up. What is right?
a: Ask if he needs help and fetch adults
Pull him up hard by the arm
129896.e: Someone who has fallen may be injured. You ask kindly and fetch adults who can call the emergency number.
129896.m: After a fall, ask and get help.

129897.q: What is important after a road accident if you want to help?
a: First make sure you are safe yourself
Run into the middle of the road
129897.e: Helpers must not put themselves in danger. First you check that it is safe and fetch adults.
129897.m: When helping, think of your own safety first.

129898.q: What does health insurance definitely not pay for?
129898.e: Health insurance helps with illness and treatment. You buy a new bike yourself.
129898.m: Health insurance pays only for health.

129899.q: Lara needed a small plaster. Does she have to go to hospital for that?
a: No, that can be done at home
129899.e: You treat small wounds yourself with the home first aid kit. That is quick and costs little.
129899.m: Small wounds are treated at home.

129900.q: What does a family do after major water damage in the flat?
a: Report the damage to the insurance
Say nothing for a long time
129900.e: The insurance must know about the damage so it can help. Photos of the damage are useful.
129900.m: Report damage to the insurance quickly.

129901.q: What is a doctor called who specialises in children?
129901.e: A paediatrician treats babies, children and teenagers. She knows childhood illnesses well.
129901.m: The paediatrician is there for children.

129902.q: Basic insurance is “obligatory”. What does that mean?
a: You are not allowed to have it
You get it as a present
You only need it in winter
129902.e: Obligatory means compulsory. Everyone who lives in Switzerland must have basic insurance.

129903.q: Is personal liability insurance required by law for everyone in Switzerland?
a: No, it is optional but highly recommended
129903.e: Unlike basic health insurance, personal liability insurance is optional. But because damage to others can be very expensive, almost every household has it.
129903.m: Personal liability is optional but important.

129904.q: Which insurance must every car in Switzerland have so that it may be driven?
129904.e: Without motor vehicle liability insurance a car gets no number plates. It pays for damage you cause to others with the car.

129905.q: Why do many landlords require tenants to have personal liability insurance?
a: So that damage to the flat can be paid for
So that the rent goes down
Because otherwise the electricity does not work
Because the municipality always demands it
129905.e: If a tenant makes a hole in the kitchen worktop, for example, liability insurance can cover the damage. That protects the landlord.
129905.m: Tenants usually need personal liability insurance.

129906.q: What does personal liability insurance not pay for when you move out of a rented flat?
a: Normal wear and tear from living there
A burn hole in the carpet
A scratch in the parquet from a cupboard that fell over
129906.e: Walls going slightly yellow after years or floors being a little worn is normal wear and tear. Nobody has to pay compensation for that.
129906.m: Normal wear and tear is not damage.

129907.q: Since the bike vignette was abolished, who usually pays when a cyclist damages a car?
129907.e: The bike vignette was abolished in 2012. Since then personal liability insurance covers damage you cause by bike.
129907.m: Bike damage to others is paid by personal liability.

129908.q: What happens if someone without liability insurance causes expensive damage to others?
a: They have to pay for the damage themselves
129908.e: Whoever causes damage is liable for it. Without insurance you have to pay with your own money, even if it is a lot.
129908.m: Without liability insurance you pay the damage yourself.

129909.q: What is the difference between household contents and liability insurance?
a: Contents pays for your own things, liability for damage to others
Contents is for the car, liability for the bike
129909.e: Household contents insurance protects your own belongings. Liability insurance steps in when you cause damage to others.
129909.m: Contents: my things. Liability: damage to others.

129910.q: How are children usually covered by personal liability insurance?
a: With their own policy from birth
129910.e: Many families have personal liability insurance for the whole household. The children are covered by it too.
129910.m: Children are often in the family liability policy.

129911.q: In household contents insurance, what is the sum insured?
a: The amount up to which your things are insured
129911.e: The sum insured should be roughly as high as the value of all the things in the flat. The insurance pays up to this amount.
129911.m: The sum insured is the maximum covered.

129912.q: Why should the sum insured for household contents match the value of your things?
a: Otherwise the insurance pays less in a claim
Otherwise you get no more post
129912.e: If the sum is too low, it is called underinsurance. Then the insurer reduces the payment in a claim.
129912.m: Too low a sum means underinsurance.

a: Damage caused by forces of nature such as floods or storms
Damage from falling off a bike
129913.e: Natural hazards include floods, storms, hail, avalanches and landslides, for example. In Switzerland they are usually covered by contents and buildings insurance.
129913.m: Forces of nature cause natural hazard damage.

129914.q: Which insurance do homeowners need for their house, compulsory in most cantons?
129914.e: Buildings insurance pays for damage to the house, from fire or flooding for example. It is compulsory in most cantons.
129914.m: The house is insured by buildings insurance.

129915.q: Lea lives in a rented flat. Who insures the building?
129915.e: The owner takes care of the building. Lea only insures her own things with household contents insurance.
129915.m: Tenants insure contents, owners the building.

129916.q: After a break-in the family has called the police. What do they do next?
a: Report the damage to the household contents insurance
129916.e: Household contents insurance pays for stolen things. For this it often needs confirmation from the police and a list of the items.

129917.q: Why do you keep receipts for expensive items such as a laptop or bike?
a: To prove their value in a claim
So you can give them away
129917.e: After a theft or fire the insurer wants to know what the things cost. Receipts are the best proof.

129918.q: Jonas's locked bike is stolen at the station. What does he usually need in his contents insurance for this?
a: Cover for simple theft away from home
The accident cover of his health insurance
129918.e: Theft outside the home is often an add-on in household contents insurance. You have to choose it deliberately.
129918.m: Theft away from home is often an add-on.

129919.q: The contents insurance says “excess 200 francs”. What does that mean?
a: You pay 200 francs of every claim yourself
The insurance pays at most 200 francs
The premium costs 200 francs a month
You get 200 francs as a gift
129919.e: The excess is a fixed part of the damage that you bear yourself. The insurance pays the rest.
129919.m: You pay the excess yourself on every claim.

129920.q: What is legal expenses insurance for?
a: It helps with the costs of lawyers and courts
129920.e: In a dispute, with a landlord or a company for example, lawyers and courts can be expensive. Legal expenses insurance covers such costs.
129920.m: Legal expenses insurance helps in legal disputes.

129921.q: What does cancellation insurance pay for?
a: Costs if you have to cancel a trip because of illness
The flight if you no longer feel like going
129921.e: If you fall ill or have an accident before departure, you cannot go on the trip. The insurance then pays the cancellation costs.
129921.m: Cancellation insurance pays if illness stops a trip.

a: Telling the insurer that damage has happened
129922.e: With the claim report the insurer learns what happened, when and where. Today this is often done online.
129922.m: You report damage to the insurer.

129923.q: What is the person called who takes out an insurance policy and pays the premium?
129923.e: The policyholder signs the contract and pays the premium. Other people can also be insured, such as the children.
129923.m: Whoever signs the contract is the policyholder.

129924.q: Many families are Rega patrons. What does that mean?
a: They support the Rega air rescue with a yearly contribution
They no longer pay health insurance
129924.e: The Rega is largely funded by its patrons. If the insurers do not pay for a mission, the Rega can waive the costs for patrons.
129924.m: Patrons support the Rega every year.

129925.q: A child with a deductible (Franchise) of 0 francs has a bill of 80 francs. How much do the parents pay?
129925.e: With no deductible, the 10 per cent co-payment applies straight away. 10 per cent of 80 francs is 8 francs.
129925.m: Co-payment: 10 per cent of the bill.

129926.q: Mr Frei has a deductible (Franchise) of 1000 francs. During the year he gets bills of 400 and 700 francs. How much does he pay himself?
129926.e: Together that is 1100 francs. The first 1000 francs are the deductible; of the remaining 100 francs he pays 10 per cent, so 10 francs.
129926.m: First the deductible, then 10 per cent co-payment.

129927.q: Does the basic health insurance premium depend on income?
a: No, it does not depend on your wage
Yes, people who earn more pay more
Yes, it is one per cent of your wage
129927.e: In Switzerland you pay a flat per-person premium, regardless of wage. But people on low incomes can get premium reductions.
129927.m: The premium does not depend on your wage.

129928.q: What affects the amount of the basic insurance premium?
a: Place of residence, age, deductible and model
129928.e: The premium depends on the insurer, the premium region, the age group, the deductible and the chosen model. Health, wage and sex play no part.
129928.m: Place, age, deductible and model set the premium.

a: It nurses and cares for people at home
129929.e: Spitex helps ill, elderly or injured people in their homes. Care prescribed by a doctor is covered by basic insurance.

129930.q: Does basic insurance pay for psychotherapy with a psychologist?
a: Yes, if a doctor has ordered it
Only if you pay in cash
129930.e: Psychological psychotherapy is paid by basic insurance if a doctor orders it. Mental health is just as important as physical health.
129930.m: Basic insurance pays for psychotherapy ordered by a doctor.

129931.q: Who normally writes a prescription for a prescription-only medicine?
129931.e: Prescription-only medicines must be prescribed by a medical professional, usually the doctor. You take the prescription to the pharmacy.
129931.m: Prescriptions are usually written by the doctor.

129932.q: Why does the pharmacy often ask whether you would like a generic?
a: Because it works the same and costs less
Because generics never have side effects
129932.e: Generics contain the same active ingredient as the original and are cheaper. That saves money for you and the health insurer.

a: An unwanted effect of a medicine
The main effect of a medicine
129933.e: Besides the desired effect, a medicine can also have other consequences, such as tiredness. They are listed in the package leaflet.
129933.m: Side effects are listed in the package leaflet.

129934.q: A person is unconscious but breathing normally. What position do you put them in after the emergency call?
129934.e: In the recovery position the airway stays clear and vomit can drain out. Until the rescuers arrive, you keep checking the breathing.

129935.q: May someone without medical training use a defibrillator?
a: Yes, the device says exactly what to do
Only with a permit from the municipality
129935.e: An automated external defibrillator, or AED, gives spoken instructions. It only gives a shock if one is needed.

129936.q: A person does not respond and is not breathing normally. What do you do after calling 144?
a: Shake them until they wake up
129936.e: In a cardiac arrest every minute counts. With chest compressions and a defibrillator you can save a life.

129937.q: Which course do you need in Switzerland before you get your learner's permit for a car?
129937.e: Anyone who wants to learn to drive must attend a first aid course. There you learn how to help properly at an accident.
129937.m: No first aid course, no learner's permit.

129938.q: Which sign can point to a stroke?
a: A drooping corner of the mouth and sudden speech problems
Cold feet after a winter walk
129938.e: In a stroke the face, an arm or speech is suddenly affected. Then you call 144 at once, because fast treatment is crucial.

129939.q: In the Telmed model, when can you reach the medical advice line by phone?
a: Around the clock, even at night
129939.e: Telemedical advice is available day and night all year round. It tells you whether to go to the doctor, the pharmacy or A&E.
129939.m: Telmed can be reached around the clock.

129940.q: Your family doctor is on holiday. Where do you go in the family doctor model?
a: To the stand-in doctor she names
To the pharmacy for an operation
129940.e: Family doctors have a stand-in when they are away. You may go to that doctor even in the family doctor model.

129941.q: What is an accident called that employees have in their free time?
129941.e: An accident at work is an occupational accident. An accident playing sport at the weekend is a non-occupational accident.

129942.q: Which large accident insurer covers many employees in industry and construction?
129942.e: Suva is the largest accident insurer in Switzerland. Many companies in industry, construction and trade are insured with it.
129942.m: Many employees have accident insurance with Suva.

129943.q: When checking a doctor's bill, what do you look at first?
a: Whether the name and date of treatment are correct
129943.e: If there is a wrong name or a date when you were not there, something is wrong. Then you look at the individual services.

129944.q: The same doctor's visit appears twice on a bill. What do you do?
a: Ask the surgery whether it was charged twice
129944.e: Mistakes on bills happen. You ask politely so that the bill gets corrected.

129945.q: How can you conveniently pay a bill with a QR code?
a: Scan the code with the banking app
Copy out the code and post it
Cut out the code and stick it on
Go to the cinema with the code
129945.e: The QR code contains the account, the amount and the reference. The banking app reads everything in; you only have to confirm.
129945.m: Scan the QR code and pay.

129946.q: What can you do if you cannot pay a large doctor's bill all at once?
a: Ask early and request payment in instalments
129946.e: If you talk to them early, there is often a solution, such as paying in instalments. That way you avoid reminders.

129947.q: Why does the health insurance premium belong firmly in a budget?
a: Because you definitely have to pay it every month
Because it is different every month
129947.e: The premium is a fixed expense that comes every month. That is why you plan it into the budget from the start.
129947.m: The premium is a fixed expense.

129948.q: Why do many people put money aside for the deductible (Franchise)?
a: So they can pay doctor's bills
129948.e: Until the deductible is reached, you pay the costs yourself. With savings you will not get into money trouble.
129948.m: Put money aside for the deductible.

129949.q: What does “treated as an outpatient” mean?
129949.e: With outpatient treatment you go home the same day. That is often cheaper than a hospital stay.

129950.q: What does “inpatient” mean in a hospital?
a: You stay in hospital for at least one night
You only get advice by phone
You go home after an hour
129950.e: Inpatient means you get a bed in hospital and stay the night there. Outpatient is the opposite.
129950.m: Inpatient means with an overnight stay.

129951.q: What is a referral at the doctor's?
a: The family doctor sends you to a specialist
129951.e: If you need a specialist, the family doctor writes a referral. In the family doctor model this is usually required.
129951.m: A referral leads to the specialist.

a: A doctor for a particular field, such as skin
A doctor who only works at weekends
A doctor who only treats animals
129952.e: Specialists have focused on one field, such as skin, eyes or ears. The family doctor, by contrast, knows the whole person.
129952.m: Specialist doctors are experts in one field.

129953.q: Whom do you call if you are ill at night but it is not life-threatening?
a: Nobody, you go to work tomorrow
129953.e: For urgent but not life-threatening cases there is an out-of-hours medical service in every region. 144 is for real emergencies.

129954.q: What is an inventory for household contents insurance?
a: A list of your things and their value
129954.e: In an inventory you write down which things you own and roughly what they are worth. That way you can set the right sum insured.
129954.m: The inventory lists your household contents.

129955.q: The Weber family moves to a bigger flat and buys lots of new furniture. What should they do about their contents insurance?
a: Check and adjust the sum insured
129955.e: With lots of new furniture the value of the household contents rises. Without an adjustment there is a risk of underinsurance in a claim.
129955.m: Adjust the sum after new purchases.

129956.q: What does a moped need so you may ride it on the road?
a: A number plate with liability insurance
129956.e: A moped needs a number plate. This comes with liability insurance that pays for damage to others.
129956.m: Mopeds need a plate and liability insurance.

129957.q: On the slope Nico crashes into another skier and her skis break. Who pays for the skis?
129957.e: Nico caused the damage to another person. His personal liability insurance is responsible for that.
129957.m: Damage to others on the slopes: liability insurance.

129958.q: Do you already have to pay the co-payment while the deductible (Franchise) is not yet used up?
a: No, it only comes after the deductible
129958.e: First you pay the costs yourself up to the deductible. Only on costs above that is the 10 per cent co-payment added.
129958.m: First the deductible, then the co-payment.

129959.q: From what age does the lowest adult deductible (Franchise) of 300 francs apply in basic insurance?
129959.e: Up to age 18 the rules for children apply, with deductibles starting at 0 francs. From 19 the deductible starts at 300 francs.
129959.m: From 19 the deductible starts at 300 francs.

129960.q: What is the advantage of a low deductible (Franchise)?
a: The insurer starts sharing the costs sooner
The premium is at its lowest
You never have to pay anything again
You may have a private room
129960.e: With a low deductible the premium is higher, but the insurer starts paying after only small costs. That suits people who see the doctor often.
