It is the password to open it
130218.e: With the tracking number you can see online whether the parcel is on its way or has arrived.

130219.q: What does a “No advertising” sticker on the letterbox do?
a: Unaddressed advertising is no longer delivered
130219.e: With the sticker, advertising without a name is no longer put in. Addressed letters still arrive.

130220.q: Where on a letter is the sender's address written?
a: Top left or on the back
130220.e: The recipient's address goes on the right. You write the sender top left or on the back.
130220.m: Sender top left or on the back.

130221.q: A letter is going to 1201 Geneva. In which part of Switzerland are places with postcodes from 1000?
130221.e: Postcodes starting with 1 belong to western Switzerland, for example Geneva, Lausanne or Fribourg.

130222.q: Postcodes starting with 8 are mainly in which area?
130222.e: Zurich has postcodes from 8000. Many surrounding places also start with 8.

130223.q: Why do you send an important letter by registered post?
a: So you can prove it was sent and delivered
So it goes without a stamp
So nobody may open it, not even the recipient
130223.e: With registered post you get a receipt and the delivery is recorded. This is important for notices of cancellation.
130223.m: Send important letters by registered post.

130224.q: What is the best way to put an empty PET bottle in the collection?
a: Squash it flat and screw the lid back on
130224.e: Squashed bottles take up less space. With the lid on, they stay flat.

130225.q: What do you remove from a jar before putting it in the glass collection?
130225.e: Metal lids cause problems when glass is melted down and belong in the scrap metal.
130225.m: Lid off, jar in the collection.

130226.q: Why may you not throw glass into many collection points on Sundays?
a: Because of the noise for the neighbours
Because glass only melts on Mondays
130226.e: Throwing in glass is noisy. That is why many municipalities have set times and Sunday rest.
130226.m: Only throw in glass at the permitted times.

130227.q: What do you do with old frying oil?
a: Let it cool and take it to a collection point
130227.e: Oil blocks pipes and pollutes water. Many municipalities collect used oil separately.
130227.m: Never pour old oil down the sink.

130228.q: Where do leftover paint or chemicals go?
a: To the hazardous waste collection point or back to the shop
130228.e: Paints and chemicals are toxic. They are disposed of in a special way.

130229.q: May you burn rubbish in your own garden in Switzerland?
a: Yes, if there is no wind
Yes, if you tell the neighbours
130229.e: Burning rubbish produces toxic substances. Household waste belongs in the waste incineration plant.

130230.q: What do you do with used aluminium coffee capsules?
a: Take them to a capsule collection point
Throw them in the glass collection
Put them in the paper collection
130230.e: Aluminium capsules can be recycled. There are collection points for them in shops and municipalities.
130230.m: Aluminium capsules go to the capsule collection.

130231.q: Where do you find out when paper and cardboard are collected in your municipality?
130231.e: The municipality publishes a waste calendar, often also online or as an app.
130231.m: Collection days are in the waste calendar.

130232.q: What does “best before” on a pack mean?
a: The product is often still fine afterwards; you check it
You must throw it away on that day
It is only edible from that day
The shop must then give it away free
130232.e: After the date you can look, smell and taste. With “use by”, for meat for example, the date is strict.
130232.m: Best before does not mean bad straight away.

130233.q: Fresh mince says “use by”. What does that mean?
a: You should not eat it after this date
You may only eat it from this date
130233.e: Perishable foods can make you ill after this date.
130233.m: Use by: take the date seriously.

130234.q: A jacket costs 80 francs. There is 25 per cent off. How much does it cost now?
130234.e: 25 per cent of 80 francs is 20 francs. 80 minus 20 is 60 francs.
130234.m: Work out the discount first, then subtract it.

130235.q: Pack A: 500 g of rice for 2 francs. Pack B: 1 kg of rice for 3 francs. Which is cheaper per kilo?
130235.e: Pack A costs 4 francs per kilo, pack B only 3 francs.
130235.m: The price per kilo is a fair comparison.

130236.q: Why does the price label often show a price per 100 g or per litre?
a: So you can compare packs of different sizes
Because you may only buy 100 g
So you know how heavy the shop is
130236.e: The unit price shows what the same amount of goods costs. So you can see whether the big pack really is cheaper.
130236.m: The unit price helps you compare.

130237.q: What do many people in Switzerland use the Twint app for?
a: To pay with their phone or send money
130237.e: With Twint you pay in shops or online and can send money to friends.

130238.q: Why is it worth glancing at the receipt after shopping?
a: To spot price mistakes or items scanned twice
Because otherwise you may not throw it away
Because homework is written on it
130238.e: Mistakes happen at the till too. If you check straight away, you can sort them out at once.

130239.q: Why are sweets often placed right by the till in shops?
a: So people grab them on impulse while waiting
So they are easier to return
130239.e: While waiting you see the sweets and often buy them without having planned to. This is called an impulse buy.
130239.m: Before buying, think: do I need this?

130240.q: What number does Die Dargebotene Hand, the Swiss helpline that listens when you are worried, have?
130240.e: On 143 you can reach people who listen, around the clock. For children and young people there is also 147.

130241.q: Why does the emergency centre ask so many questions on the phone?
a: So it can send the right help to the right place
Because it wants to fill time
Because it wants to test you
Because it is writing a newspaper report
130241.e: The place, the type of emergency and the number of injured help to send the right help quickly.

130242.q: When are the sirens tested every year in Switzerland?
a: On the first Wednesday in February
On the last day of the year
130242.e: Once a year they check that all sirens work. There is no reason to worry then.
130242.m: Siren test: first Wednesday in February.

130243.q: The siren wails up and down, and it is not a test. What do you do?
a: Listen to the radio or read Alertswiss and follow the instructions
Get straight into the car and drive away
Call the emergency numbers to ask
130243.e: In a general alarm, the radio and Alertswiss tell you what to do. Emergency numbers are for real emergencies.
130243.m: Siren: get informed and follow instructions.

130244.q: A small fire is burning in the waste paper basket. What helps well while it is still small?
a: A fire blanket or a fire extinguisher
A sheet of paper on top
Opening the door wide to air the room
130244.e: Small fires can be smothered with a fire blanket or extinguisher. If it gets bigger, get out and call 118.
130244.m: Small fire: put it out. Big fire: get out and call 118.

130245.q: An email looks as if it is from your bank and asks for your password. What is this fraud called?
130245.e: Fraudsters pretend to be a bank, the post or a company so that you enter passwords or card details. Banks never ask for your password by email.
130245.m: No bank asks for your password by email.

130246.q: Why should you install updates for your phone and apps?
a: Because otherwise the phone gets heavier
Because then you get more credit
130246.e: Updates fix flaws that attackers could exploit.

130247.q: What should you avoid doing on open Wi-Fi in a café?
a: Logging into e-banking with your password
130247.e: On open networks others may be able to read along. For sensitive things it is better to use your own network.
130247.m: No sensitive logins on open Wi-Fi.

130248.q: What does roaming mean for a mobile phone?
a: Abroad the phone uses a foreign network, which can be expensive
The phone switches off the sound
The phone saves photos in the cloud
130248.e: Abroad, data and calls can cost a lot. Before travelling it is worth checking the settings.

130249.q: Why should you not share your live location publicly?
a: Strangers could see where you are right now
Because the battery then fills up
Because the photos then get blurry
130249.e: You share your location at most with family and close friends you trust.
130249.m: My location is only for people I trust.

130250.q: Why do you think carefully before posting a photo online?
a: Because it can be copied and stays findable for a long time
Because otherwise the photo gets blurry
130250.e: Even deleted pictures may already have been saved or forwarded.
130250.m: What goes online often stays forever.

130251.q: You read an unbelievable story online. How do you check whether it is true?
a: Look it up in several well-known sources
Only look at the number of likes
Believe the sender because they sound sure
130251.e: If reputable media are not reporting it, be careful.

130252.q: For which journeys on Swiss public transport do you need a ticket before you board?
a: For almost every journey by bus, tram and train
130252.e: In Switzerland you normally buy your ticket before travelling. Anyone without one has to pay a surcharge when checked.

130253.q: What is the best way to air a flat in winter?
a: Open the windows wide for a short time several times a day
Leave the window tilted open all day
Never air it, so it stays warm
Only leave the door open at night
130253.e: With short, wide-open airing, fresh air comes in quickly without the walls cooling down. That helps against mould.
130253.m: Air briefly and wide instead of tilting the window.

130254.q: Which temperature is often recommended for living rooms and bedrooms?
a: About 20 degrees in the living room, a little cooler in the bedroom
130254.e: Every degree lower saves heating energy. 20 degrees in living areas is considered comfortable.

130255.q: What is not allowed on Sundays in many Swiss municipalities?
a: Mowing the lawn with a motor mower
130255.e: In many municipalities Sunday is a day of rest. Noisy work such as mowing the lawn is forbidden then.

130256.q: Where does it say what is allowed in a block of flats, for example when you may do your washing?
130256.e: The house rules govern living together, such as quiet times, the laundry room or the bike cellar.
130256.m: The house rules govern living together in the building.

130257.q: You are having a party at home on Saturday. What is considerate?
a: Tell the neighbours beforehand and respect the night-time quiet
Say nothing and party loudly until morning
Point the music out of the window
130257.e: Letting people know beforehand shows consideration. Night-time quiet still applies.
130257.m: Announce the party, respect night-time quiet.

130258.q: The neighbour often plays loud music late at night. What is a good first step?
a: Talk to him in a friendly way
Stick an angry note on his door
130258.e: Many people do not even know they are disturbing others. A calm conversation often solves the problem.

130259.q: In a family or shared flat there is a chores rota (Ämtliplan). What is on it?
a: Who gets how much pocket money
130259.e: With the chores rota, jobs like washing up, cleaning or taking out the rubbish are shared fairly.

130260.q: In German-speaking Switzerland, how do you address an adult you do not know?
a: Not at all, you just wave
130260.e: You use the polite “Sie” with adults you do not know. Only when they offer “du” do you switch.
130260.m: I use the polite form with adults I do not know.

130261.q: Do you have to tip in a restaurant in Switzerland?
a: No, service is included in the price; tipping is voluntary
130261.e: In Switzerland service is included in the price. If you were happy, you often round up.

130262.q: How do you greet the trainer politely on a taster placement?
a: With eye contact, a handshake and “Grüezi”
With no greeting, straight in with a question
With your hands in your pockets
130262.e: A friendly greeting with eye contact makes a good first impression. “Grüezi” is the polite Swiss German hello.

130263.q: When is it best to arrive for a job interview?
a: About 5 to 10 minutes before the appointment
An hour early in the office
Whenever you like, as long as it is the right day
130263.e: If you arrive a few minutes early, you arrive calm and on time.

130264.q: Your bus is late and you will be late for training. What do you do?
a: Quickly let them know you will be late
Say nothing and hope nobody notices
130264.e: Getting in touch shows respect. The others do not have to wait or worry.

130265.q: What is the subject line of an email for?
a: It says briefly what the email is about
130265.e: With a clear subject the person knows at once what it is about, for example “Question about the taster placement”.

130266.q: How do you start an email to a company if you do not know the person's name?
130266.e: Formal emails and letters start politely. If you know the name, you write “Dear Ms …” or “Dear Mr …”.

130267.q: How do you usually end a formal email?
a: With no greeting and no name
130267.e: “Kind regards” is the usual ending. Then come your first name and surname.

130268.q: How is 5 March 2026 usually written in figures in Switzerland?
130268.e: In Switzerland the day comes first, then the month, then the year, separated by full stops.

130269.q: A Swiss form asks for “Name” and “Vorname” (first name). What do you write under “Name”?
130269.e: On a form, “Name” means your family name, for example “Müller”.

130270.q: In an online form a field is marked with an asterisk (*). What does that usually mean?
a: This field must be filled in
This field must not be filled in
130270.e: The asterisk marks required fields. Without them you often cannot send the form.

130271.q: Why do you read a form carefully before signing it?
a: Because by signing you confirm that you agree
Because otherwise you have to sign twice
130271.e: Anyone who signs is bound by what they signed. So read first and ask if anything is unclear.

130272.q: Nina has training, homework and a doctor's appointment in the same week. What helps her?
a: Writing all appointments in a diary
Just remembering everything in her head
Doing all appointments on the same day
Planning nothing and seeing what happens
130272.e: In a paper diary or on the phone you see all appointments at a glance.

130273.q: How do you make sure you do not forget an important appointment?
a: Set a reminder on your phone
130273.e: A reminder alerts you in good time before the appointment.

130274.q: Lina spends three days in a joinery workshop to get to know the job. What is this called?
130274.e: On a taster placement you experience everyday working life and find out whether the job suits you. The company also gets to know you.
130274.m: A taster placement shows whether a job suits you.

130275.q: What belongs in an application file for an apprenticeship?
a: Cover letter, CV and school reports
130275.e: In the file you introduce yourself: why you want the job, what you can do and what marks you have.

130276.q: What do you explain in the cover letter?
a: Why you want exactly this job and company
How much pocket money you have
130276.e: The cover letter shows that you have thought about the job and the company.
130276.m: Show your motivation: why this job?

130277.q: Which information does not belong in the CV for an apprenticeship?
130277.e: The CV shows personal details, schools, taster placements, languages and hobbies. Passwords do not belong anywhere.
130277.m: The CV shows my path briefly and clearly.

130278.q: Where do young people in Switzerland get help with choosing a career?
130278.e: At the BIZ and the careers advice service there is information about jobs and help finding an apprenticeship.
130278.m: The BIZ helps with career choice.

130279.q: What is special about an apprenticeship in Switzerland?
a: You learn at the company and attend vocational school
You only work, with no school
130279.e: An apprenticeship combines work at the training company with lessons at vocational school. This is called dual vocational training.

130280.q: Leon is turned down for an apprenticeship. What is a good reaction?
a: Keep applying and perhaps ask what he could improve
Write the company an angry email
130280.e: Rejections are part of it. Asking can help improve the next application.

130281.q: What do you do with your phone during a job interview?
a: Switch it off or to silent and put it away
Put it on the table and read messages
130281.e: That shows you are fully concentrating on the interview.
130281.m: In an interview the phone is away.

130282.q: You have lost the key to the rented flat. Whom do you inform?
a: The property management or the landlord
130282.e: A lost key can be a security risk. The management decides whether the lock is replaced.

130283.q: Where is the best place to leave your bike in a block of flats?
a: In the bike cellar or at the bike stand
130283.e: Bikes in the stairwell block the way. There are bike rooms or stands for that.

130284.q: You cut your finger slightly while chopping vegetables. What do you do?
a: Clean the wound and put on a plaster
130284.e: You clean small cuts and cover them. With heavy bleeding you press firmly and get help.
130284.m: Small wound: clean it and put on a plaster.

130285.q: A bee stings you on the arm. What usually helps?
a: Carefully remove the sting and cool the spot
Pour hot water over the spot
130285.e: Cooling eases the swelling. With breathing problems or a sting in the mouth, call 144 at once.
130285.m: Cool a sting; with breathing problems call 144.

130286.q: You see a bike accident on the road. What do you do first?
a: Secure the scene so nothing more happens
Film a video for the internet
Take the bike away and go home
130286.e: The order is: look, think, act. First secure the scene, then raise the alarm and help.

130287.q: After a walk in the woods you find a tick on your skin. What is right?
a: Pull it straight out with tweezers close to the skin
Pour oil over it and wait
130287.e: The sooner the tick is removed, the better. Afterwards you watch the spot for a few weeks.

130288.q: Why do you wear sun cream outdoors in summer?
a: So your skin does not get sunburnt
130288.e: Sunburn damages the skin. Sun cream, a hat and shade protect it.

130289.q: What belongs in a simple home first aid kit?
130289.e: With plasters, bandages, scissors and disinfectant you can treat small injuries yourself.
130289.m: Plasters and bandages belong in the first aid kit.

130290.q: In the group chat a classmate is being laughed at. What can you do?
a: Not join in and tell a trusted adult
Laugh along so you fit in
130290.e: Not joining in and getting help can stop bullying.
130290.m: With bullying, do not join in; get help.

a: Purchases with real money inside a game or app
130291.e: Many free games make money from purchases in the game. Small amounts can quickly add up.

130292.q: Why do you not use the same password for all your accounts?
a: If it is cracked, all your accounts are in danger
Because otherwise the phone gets slower
Because otherwise it gets too long
130292.e: With a stolen password, fraudsters try many websites. A separate password for each account protects you.
130292.m: A separate password for every account.

130293.q: A competition asks for your name, date of birth, address and mobile number. What is wise?
a: Think carefully about whether you want to give so much data
130293.e: Data is valuable. Some competitions collect it for advertising.
130293.m: Give only as much data as necessary.

130294.q: How do you save electricity with the TV and games console?
a: Switch them off completely instead of leaving them on standby
Cover the device with a cloth
130294.e: Devices use electricity even on standby. A power strip with a switch helps.

130295.q: How do you save energy when cooking pasta?
a: With a lid on the pan
Without a lid on the highest setting for a long time
In a pan that is far too big
With the oven on next to it
130295.e: With a lid the water boils faster and less heat is lost.
130295.m: Cooking with a lid saves energy.

130296.q: What does the care label in a T-shirt show?
a: How to wash and look after it
130296.e: The symbols show, for example, the washing temperature or whether it can go in the tumble dryer.

130297.q: Mia gets 40 francs pocket money a month and wants to save 10 francs. How much can she spend?
130297.e: 40 francs minus 10 francs savings leaves 30 francs to spend.

130298.q: What must a bike have on Swiss roads, among other things?
a: Two brakes, reflectors and a bell
130298.e: A roadworthy bike has a front and rear brake, reflectors and a bell, and lights at night.

130299.q: What applies to children who are allowed to ride their bikes on the pavement?
a: They are considerate and pedestrians have priority
They always have priority on the pavement
They may ride as fast as they like there
They must ring until everyone moves aside
130299.e: On the pavement pedestrians come first. Children on bikes adapt to them.
130299.m: On the pavement, pedestrians have priority.

130300.q: Where do you put a big suitcase on the train?
a: On the luggage rack or in the luggage area
On a seat when many people are standing
130300.e: Suitcases in the aisle or in front of the door block the way and can become an obstacle.
130300.m: Luggage on the rack, aisle clear.

130301.q: What is a good idea after a taster placement?
a: Thank the company for the time
Send the colleagues photos of them
Send an invoice for the work
130301.e: A short thank you by email or letter leaves a good impression in case you apply later.
130301.m: Saying thank you leaves a good impression.

130302.q: A jar is blue. Which container does it go in at most collection points?
130302.e: There is no separate container for blue and other coloured glass. It usually goes with the green glass.
130302.m: Coloured glass usually goes with the green glass.

130303.q: The landlord wants to raise the rent. How must he notify this?
a: With an officially approved form and a reason
With a notice in the cellar
130303.e: A rent increase is only valid if it is notified on the official form with a reason. Otherwise it is void.
130303.m: Rent increase only with the official form.

130304.q: Within what period can you challenge a rent increase at the conciliation authority?
a: At any time during the tenancy
130304.e: If you think an increase is unfair, you must challenge it within 30 days. After that it counts as accepted.

130305.q: Where do you turn first in a dispute with the landlord about the rent?
a: To the conciliation authority for tenancy matters
Straight to the Federal Supreme Court
130305.e: The conciliation authority tries to find an agreement. The procedure there is usually free of charge.
130305.m: Rent dispute: first go to the conciliation authority.

130306.q: Sven thinks the rent for his new flat is unfairly high. What can he do?
a: Challenge the initial rent within 30 days of taking over the flat
Just pay less without saying anything
Only challenge the rent after five years
Nothing, the initial rent can never be challenged
130306.e: Under certain conditions, such as hardship or a sharp increase compared with the previous tenant, you can challenge the initial rent within 30 days.
130306.m: Challenge the initial rent: within 30 days.

130307.q: The heating in the rented flat fails for weeks in winter. What can the tenant demand?
a: A rent reduction for as long as the defect lasts
A new flat from the municipality
130307.e: With a defect that limits use, you can demand repair and a rent reduction. You report the defect in writing.
130307.m: Major defect: ask for a rent reduction.

130308.q: In what form must a tenant give notice on their flat?
130308.e: Notice on a flat must be given in writing and signed. It is best sent by registered post.
130308.m: Giving notice on a flat: in writing and signed.

130309.q: After moving out, the landlord does not get in touch. When does the bank release the rent deposit if no proceedings are under way?
a: One year after the end of the tenancy
Immediately on the day you move out
130309.e: If the landlord has made no claims within a year, the tenant can ask the bank to return the deposit.
130309.m: Deposit: back after one year at the latest.

130310.q: What must the landlord do at the flat handover if he finds damage?
a: Report it to the tenant immediately
Only report it after three years
Nothing, he can claim everything later
130310.e: The landlord must report defects immediately, otherwise he usually loses his claims, except for hidden defects.
130310.m: Record damage at the handover immediately.

130311.q: After eight years of tenancy the walls are slightly yellowed. Does the tenant have to pay for repainting?
a: No, the tenant does not pay for normal wear and tear
130311.e: Normal wear and tear is covered by the rent. You only pay for damage beyond normal use.
130311.m: Normal wear and tear is included in the rent.

130312.q: The service charge statement seems too high to you. What may you ask for?
a: A cash payment from the neighbour
The statement for the whole neighbourhood
That the heating be switched off
130312.e: Tenants have the right to inspect the receipts behind the service charge statement.
130312.m: Service charges: I have the right to see the receipts.

130313.q: Which costs may a landlord not charge as service charges?
a: The interest on the building's mortgage
130313.e: Service charges are costs for services linked to use, such as heating or the caretaker. Mortgage interest is the owner's business.
130313.m: Mortgage interest is not a service charge.

130314.q: A tenant does not pay the rent. What must the landlord do before he may give notice because of this?
a: Set a written payment deadline of at least 30 days and threaten notice
Nothing, he can give notice at once
130314.e: With rent arrears the landlord must first set a written deadline of at least 30 days. Only then may he give extraordinary notice.

130315.q: May the landlord enter the flat unannounced at any time?
a: No, only with notice in good time and for a legitimate reason
Yes, he always has a key
Yes, if the tenant is on holiday
130315.e: The landlord may inspect the flat, for repairs or re-letting for example, but must announce it in good time. Exceptions apply only in emergencies.
130315.m: The landlord only comes after giving notice.

130316.q: Lena wants to paint one wall of her rented flat bright red. What does she need?
a: The signatures of all the neighbours
130316.e: Changes to the rented property are only allowed with the landlord's written consent. Otherwise you must restore the original state when moving out.
130316.m: Bigger changes only with written OK.

130317.q: What applies to a fixed-term tenancy, for example from 1 March to 31 August?
a: It ends on the agreed date without notice
It must still be cancelled three months in advance
It automatically extends by ten years
130317.e: A fixed-term contract ends without notice. If it is tacitly continued afterwards, it counts as open-ended.
130317.m: Fixed-term means it ends by itself.

130318.q: When moving into your first flat, what makes sense so you do not pay for the previous tenant?
a: Note and report the electricity and possibly gas meter readings
130318.e: With the meter reading at move-in, the energy supplier can divide up the consumption correctly.
130318.m: Note the meter reading when moving in.

130319.q: While moving in, Jan drops a bottle into the washbasin, which cracks. Which insurance usually helps?
130319.e: Damage to the rented flat, known as tenant's damage, is normally covered by personal liability insurance.

130320.q: Which rule of thumb often applies to housing costs in a budget?
a: No more than about a quarter to a third of income
130320.e: Budget advisers recommend not spending too much on rent so that enough is left for everything else.
130320.m: Rent: at most about a third of income.

130321.q: In a built-up area a scheduled bus at a stop is indicating to pull out. What applies to the cars behind it?
a: They must let it pull out
130321.e: In built-up areas you must let scheduled buses pull away from marked stops when they indicate.
130321.m: Bus indicating at a stop: let it pull out.

130322.q: When must you indicate at a roundabout?
a: The whole way round, to the left
130322.e: You do not indicate when entering. Before leaving you use the right indicator to show you are exiting.
130322.m: At a roundabout: indicate when leaving.

130323.q: Which alcohol limit generally applies to cyclists in Switzerland?
a: The same as for driving, 0.5 per mille
Only 0.0 per mille on public holidays
130323.e: Anyone cycling drunk endangers themselves and others. From 0.5 per mille you are unfit to ride, on a bike too.
130323.m: 0.5 per mille also applies on a bike.

130324.q: What has applied to motor vehicles in Switzerland during the day since 2014?
a: They must drive with lights on during the day too
They may not have lights on during the day
They must hoot during the day
They may only drive at night
130324.e: With lights on during the day, vehicles are seen earlier. Daytime running lights or dipped headlights are enough.

130325.q: A car breaks down on the motorway. At least how far behind the car do you place the warning triangle?
130325.e: On motorways it is at least 100 metres, on other roads at least 50 metres. Before that you put on the high-visibility vest.
130325.m: Warning triangle: motorway 100 m, otherwise 50 m.

130326.q: How long may you usually park in a blue zone with a parking disc on weekdays during the day?
130326.e: In the blue zone you set the parking disc to your arrival time. Usually one hour is allowed unless signs say otherwise.
130326.m: Blue zone: parking disc, usually one hour.

130327.q: What applies to fast pedal-assist e-bikes up to 45 km/h?
a: They need a number plate and a helmet
No helmet and no number plate
They may be ridden on the pavement
You may ride them from age 8
130327.e: Fast e-bikes count as mopeds with a yellow number plate. A bike helmet is compulsory.
130327.m: Fast e-bike: number plate and helmet.

130328.q: From what age may you ride a slow e-bike (up to 25 km/h) without a licence?
130328.e: Between 14 and 16 you need a category M licence for it. From 16 you do not.
130328.m: Slow e-bike: from 16 without a licence.

130329.q: Is a helmet required by law in Switzerland for ordinary bikes?
a: No, but it is strongly recommended
130329.e: There is no helmet requirement for ordinary bikes and slow e-bikes. But a helmet protects the head very effectively in a fall.
130329.m: Not compulsory, but the helmet protects.

130330.q: For how long is a seller in Switzerland legally liable for defects in new goods sold to consumers?
130330.e: The legal warranty is two years. But it can be restricted in the contract or the terms and conditions.

130331.q: You no longer like a jumper that has no faults. Must the shop take it back?
a: Yes, but only without a receipt
Yes, if you have worn it
130331.e: There is no legal right to exchange faultless goods. But many shops offer it as a goodwill gesture.

130332.q: A screen you ordered arrives with a crack. What is important?
a: Check the goods straight away and report the defect at once
Wait six months and then complain
Keep the screen and say nothing
Throw away the packaging immediately and report it later
130332.e: Anyone who receives goods must check them soon and report defects immediately. Otherwise you can lose your rights. Photos help as proof.
130332.m: Check deliveries at once, report defects at once.

130333.q: Someone sells you a subscription at the front door. Within what period can you withdraw from the contract?
130333.e: For doorstep sales and similar contracts you can withdraw in writing within 14 days.

130334.q: What must a price in a Swiss shop include?
a: VAT and all surcharges you cannot choose to avoid
130334.e: For consumers, the price actually to be paid must be displayed, including VAT.
130334.m: The displayed price is the final price.

130335.q: Can a 15-year-old take out an expensive long-term mobile phone contract without her parents' consent?
a: No, that needs the parents' consent
Yes, if she does it online
Yes, if she saves more than 100 francs
130335.e: Minors can only take on larger commitments with their parents' consent. You come of age at 18.
130335.m: Under 18, big contracts need the parents.

130336.q: What is important to know about phone numbers starting with 0900?
a: They are premium-rate services, often expensive
130336.e: Calls to 0900 numbers can cost a lot per minute. The price must be announced.

130337.q: A caller says he is from the police and wants to collect your money for safekeeping. What is true?
a: The police never ask for money or valuables on the phone
You should give him the money at once
You should give him your bank card and PIN
You should leave the front door open
130337.e: This is a well-known scam. Hang up and call 117 yourself.
130337.m: Real police do not collect money.

130338.q: Your bank's number appears on the display. Why is caution still needed?
a: Fraudsters can fake the displayed number
Banks never call from Swiss numbers
The number always shows the real caller
Banks are not allowed to phone
130338.e: With so-called spoofing, fraudsters display someone else's number. If in doubt, hang up and call the bank back on its official number.
130338.m: A displayed number is no proof.

130339.q: You are selling a bike online. The buyer sends a link where you should “receive the money” by entering your card details. What is this?
130339.e: To receive money you never need to enter card details, security codes or passwords.
130339.m: Receiving money never needs card details.

130340.q: Which feature suggests a fake online shop?
a: Payment in advance only and no legal notice with an address
Several payment methods such as invoice
Customer service with a phone number
130340.e: Fake shops lure people with low prices, demand payment in advance and hide who is behind them.
130340.m: No legal notice, advance payment only: hands off.

130341.q: Under the Unfair Competition Act, what must an online shop in Switzerland state?
a: Clear information about its identity and a contact address with email
The pay list of its employees
130341.e: Anyone selling online must say clearly who they are and how to contact them.
130341.m: Online shops must say who they are.

130342.q: What does an asterisk (*) next to an entry in the phone directory mean?
a: The person does not want advertising calls or advertising
The person can never be reached
130342.e: Companies may not contact people with an asterisk for advertising. Otherwise they act unfairly.
130342.m: Asterisk in the directory: no advertising.

130343.q: A website asks whether it may set cookies. What are cookies?
a: Small files with which the website recognises you
130343.e: Cookies store settings or a shopping basket, for example, but can also be used for advertising.
130343.m: Cookies remember something about my visit.

130344.q: There is a padlock symbol next to the web address. What does it mean?
a: The connection is encrypted; the site can still be fraudulent
The site is definitely genuine and checked by the police
130344.e: The padlock only shows that data is transmitted in encrypted form. Fraudsters use encrypted sites too.
130344.m: Padlock means encrypted, not necessarily genuine.

130345.q: What do you do before selling your old phone or taking it to a collection point?
a: Back up your data and reset the device to factory settings
Nothing, the data disappears by itself
Put the battery in the compost
130345.e: The phone holds photos, messages and logins. Resetting deletes them.

130346.q: Must a shop that sells toasters take back your old toaster even if you buy nothing new?
a: Yes, free, because the recycling fee has already been paid
No, only if you buy a new one
Only if it was bought in the same shop
130346.e: Retailers take back devices of the kind they sell free of charge. Disposal is paid for by the advance recycling fee.
130346.m: Old electrical appliances go back to the shop for free.

130347.q: What happens in Switzerland to the combustible rubbish from the rubbish bag?
a: It is burnt, and the heat is used for electricity and district heating
It is taken to the sea
130347.e: Since 2000 combustible waste may no longer go to landfill. Waste incineration plants generate energy from it.

130348.q: A water pipe bursts in the rented flat on a Sunday. What do you do first?
a: Turn off the water if possible and call the management's emergency service or the caretaker
Wait until Monday and write an email
Leave the flat and say nothing
Ask the neighbours to pay for the damage
130348.e: In an emergency such as a burst pipe you must keep the damage small and report it immediately. Many managements have an emergency number for this.
130348.m: Burst pipe: water off, report at once.

130349.q: May an empty shampoo bottle go in the PET collection?
a: No, only PET drinks bottles belong there
Yes, if it is still half full
130349.e: The PET collection is only for drinks bottles. Other plastics disrupt recycling.
130349.m: Only drinks bottles in the PET collection.

130350.q: What can be produced from collected green waste in fermentation plants?
130350.e: Fermentation produces biogas, which supplies electricity and heat. The rest becomes fertiliser or compost.
130350.m: Green waste becomes biogas and fertiliser.

130351.q: Which contract must be made in writing in Switzerland?
a: Every purchase contract in a shop
A contract for an ice cream at the kiosk
130351.e: An employment contract is valid even if made verbally. The apprenticeship contract, however, must be in writing and is approved by the canton.

130352.q: Which legal notice period applies during the probation period of an ordinary employment?
130352.e: During the probation period, employment can be ended with seven days' notice, unless otherwise agreed.

130353.q: Under the Code of Obligations, what generally applies to overtime unless otherwise agreed in writing?
a: It is paid with a 25 per cent supplement or compensated with time off
It is paid with a 100 per cent supplement
130353.e: Overtime must be compensated with wages plus at least 25 per cent, or, by agreement, with the same amount of time off.
130353.m: Overtime: 25 per cent supplement or time off.

130354.q: Under the Employment Act, what is the maximum number of hours a day that young people under 18 may work?
130354.e: Young people may work at most 9 hours a day, within a span of 12 hours. School time counts too.
130354.m: Young people: at most 9 hours a day.

130355.q: From what age may young people in Switzerland do light paid work such as running errands?
130355.e: From 13, light work that does not endanger health or school is allowed, such as babysitting or delivering newspapers.

130356.q: An apprentice wakes up with a temperature. What does he do first?
a: Inform the company before work starts
Say nothing and stay at home
Only write an email in the evening
Send a colleague without letting anyone know
130356.e: Anyone who is ill reports in sick as early as possible. Depending on the contract, a doctor's certificate is needed from a certain day.
130356.m: Ill: tell the company at once.

130357.q: What do apprentices in many trades keep during their apprenticeship?
a: A learning record of their work
A diary of their free time
130357.e: In the learning record, apprentices note what they have learned and done. It also helps them prepare for the exam.
130357.m: The learning record shows what I have learned.

130358.q: What are inter-company courses (üK) in an apprenticeship?
a: Courses outside the company for basic job skills
130358.e: The üK complement the company and the vocational school. There apprentices practise important basics of their trade.
130358.m: Apprenticeship: company, school and inter-company courses.

130359.q: You want to give your former teacher as a reference in your CV. What do you do first?
a: Write down her private address without asking
130359.e: Referees should know that they might be called. Then they can prepare.

130360.q: Why is it worth looking at your own public social media profiles before looking for an apprenticeship?
a: Because companies sometimes look up applicants online
Because otherwise you may not sign an apprenticeship contract
Because otherwise the profiles are deleted
130360.e: Embarrassing pictures or insults can make a bad impression. It is better to set profiles to private.
130360.m: My online presence is part of my application.

130361.q: What is the best way to send an application by email?
a: As one sensibly named PDF with all documents
As text with no attachment and lots of smileys
130361.e: A single PDF is clear and looks the same on every device.
130361.m: Send the application as one PDF.

130362.q: Why do you have someone proofread your cover letter?
a: So spelling mistakes and unclear sentences are spotted
Because companies may only read proofread letters
130362.e: Others spot mistakes more quickly. A letter without mistakes looks careful.
130362.m: Four eyes see more than two.

130363.q: In a job interview you are asked about a weakness. What is a good answer?
a: Name a real weakness and say how you are working on it
Not answer and look at the floor
130363.e: Honesty and the will to improve go down well.
130363.m: Name a weakness, show a solution.

130364.q: You have a job interview by video. What do you prepare?
a: A quiet place, good light and a tested camera and microphone
A game in a second window
130364.e: A video interview is as important as meeting in person. Testing the technology beforehand avoids stress.

130365.q: What do you check on your first payslip?
a: Whether wages, deductions and working hours are correct
Only the colour of the paper
Whether the boss's name is spelt correctly
130365.e: Mistakes happen on payslips too. If you check, you notice early.

130366.q: Which digits does every Swiss AHV number begin with?
130366.e: The AHV number has 13 digits and begins with 756, the country code for Switzerland.

130367.q: The advert says “net rent 1500 francs”. What does “net” mean?
130367.e: Service charges are added to the net rent. Together they make the gross rent.

130368.q: A form asks for “marital status”. What does a person who has never been married write?
130368.e: “Single” means never married or in a registered partnership.

130369.q: For some jobs, working with children for example, an extract from the criminal record is required. Where do you order it?
a: From the Federal Office of Justice, online or at the post office for example
130369.e: The private extract from the criminal record is issued by the Federal Office of Justice. You can order it online or at a post office counter.
130369.m: Criminal record extract: Federal Office of Justice.

130370.q: A legal deadline with an authority ends on a Sunday. What usually applies?
a: It is extended to the next working day
It is extended by a month
130370.e: If the end of a deadline falls on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday, it ends on the next working day.
130370.m: Deadline ending at the weekend: next working day.

130371.q: You must write to an authority within a deadline. When is a letter still on time?
a: If it is handed to Swiss Post on the last day of the deadline at the latest
Only if it arrives the day after the deadline
If it is sent a month after the deadline
Only if you hand it in personally at night
130371.e: With authorities and courts, handing it to Swiss Post on the last day usually counts. With cancellations of contracts, what often matters is when the letter arrives.
130371.m: Authority deadline: posting on the last day is enough.

130372.q: Your flatmate is to collect a registered letter for you at the post office. What does she need?
a: Authorisation from you and her ID
130372.e: With an authorisation, someone else may accept registered items for you.
130372.m: Collecting for others: authorisation and ID.

130373.q: Elena moves to another canton in October. Where does she normally pay cantonal and municipal taxes for the whole year?
a: In the canton where she lives on 31 December
In the canton where she was born
Not at all, because of the move
130373.e: For cantonal and municipal taxes, the place of residence at the end of the tax period, 31 December, generally counts.

130374.q: What do you typically include with an application for a rented flat?
a: The completed application form, a debt collection register extract and a copy of your ID
A photo of your pet as the only document
130374.e: Landlords want to see who is moving in and whether the rent can be paid.
130374.m: Flat application: form and debt register extract.

130375.q: Why do you return all keys when you move out, including copies you had made?
a: Because missing keys can mean the lock is replaced at your expense
Because the next tenant collects them
Because otherwise you have to throw them away
130375.e: If keys are missing, the landlord can replace the lock for security reasons and charge you for it.
130375.m: Return all keys when moving out.

130376.q: What applies in Switzerland if someone does not help a seriously injured person even though it would be reasonable to do so?
a: It can be a criminal offence of failing to render aid
It is rewarded with a medal
130376.e: Anyone who does not help a person in immediate danger of death, although it is reasonable for them to do so, commits an offence. Raising the alarm is already help.
130376.m: Helping is a duty; raising the alarm is already help.

130377.q: What ratio of chest compressions to rescue breaths is taught for adults?
130377.e: You press firmly on the centre of the chest 30 times and then give two breaths. Anyone who does not want to give breaths does compressions only.

130378.q: Which short number reaches roadside breakdown assistance in Switzerland?
130378.e: On 140 you reach roadside breakdown assistance. But if anyone is injured you dial 144 or 117.

130379.q: How much drinking water per person does the Confederation recommend for an emergency supply at home?
130379.e: 9 litres of water per person are recommended, about 3 litres a day for three days, plus food for about a week.
130379.m: Emergency supply: 9 litres of water per person.

130380.q: What colour are signs for emergency exits and escape routes?
130380.e: Green safety signs show the way out. Red signs show fire protection, such as fire extinguishers.

130381.q: Why is carbon monoxide, from a faulty stove for example, so dangerous?
a: It smells very strongly of smoke
It is only dangerous for plants
130381.e: You do not notice carbon monoxide. It can cause headaches, unconsciousness and death. A CO alarm gives warning.
130381.m: You cannot notice CO: an alarm helps.

130382.q: After moving you have registered with the municipality. Whom should you also tell your new address?
a: Your bank, health insurer and employer or training company
Only your friends in the chat
130382.e: The municipality does not inform everyone. So that bills and letters arrive, you pass on the address yourself.

130383.q: Why does it make sense to store an emergency contact and important health details on your phone?
a: Rescuers can see them even when the phone is locked
So strangers can unlock your phone
130383.e: Many phones show emergency contacts and allergies on the lock screen without needing the code.
130383.m: Store an emergency contact on your phone.

130384.q: What does it mean if you put someone in the “Cc” field of an email?
a: The person gets a copy for information
The person cannot read the email
The person must sign the email
130384.e: “Cc” stands for copy. All recipients can see who got the copy.

130385.q: When do you use “Reply all” on a group email?
a: Only when the reply really concerns everyone
130385.e: Unnecessary replies to everyone fill up many inboxes. Often a reply to the sender is enough.
130385.m: Reply all only if it concerns everyone.

130386.q: What is an out-of-office message in an email program for?
a: It automatically says you are away and who is covering for you
It deletes all emails during the holidays
It forwards your emails to all contacts
130386.e: That way others know they will not get an immediate reply and whom they can contact.
130386.m: On holiday: set up an out-of-office message.

130387.q: A company invites you to an interview by email. What do you do?
a: Confirm the appointment quickly and say thank you
Not reply and simply turn up
Suggest a time when the company is closed
130387.e: A quick confirmation shows interest and reliability.

130388.q: You are invited to dinner with your friend's family. What is a nice gesture?
a: Bring a small gift and say thank you afterwards
Go straight to the table without a greeting
Play on your phone while everyone eats
130388.e: A small gift such as flowers or chocolate and a thank you show appreciation.
130388.m: Invited: a small gift and a thank you.

130389.q: Your magazine subscription renews automatically. What must you watch out for if you want to end it?
a: Keep to the notice period in the contract
130389.e: Many subscriptions renew if you do not cancel in time. The notice period is in the terms of the contract.

130390.q: What is the most important difference between a debit card and a credit card?
a: The debit card charges the account directly, the credit card sends a bill later
The debit card only works abroad
The credit card is always free
With the debit card you can only withdraw cash
130390.e: With a credit card you get a monthly bill. If you do not pay it in full, you pay high interest.
130390.m: Debit: straight from the account. Credit: bill later.

130391.q: At what age do you come of age in Switzerland and can sign all contracts yourself?
130391.e: You come of age at 18. Then you are responsible for your own contracts and debts.

130392.q: What do you look out for when viewing a flat?
a: Mould, the condition of the windows and kitchen, and noise in the area
Only the colour of the walls
130392.e: At a viewing you see defects and sources of noise not mentioned in the advert. Questions about service charges and heating are worthwhile.

130393.q: What is a standing order at the bank particularly suitable for?
a: The monthly rent, which is the same amount each time
A one-off purchase in a shop
Bills with a different amount each time
130393.e: A standing order regularly pays the same amount, such as the rent at the end of the month.

130394.q: Which repair does a tenant normally have to pay for herself?
130394.e: Small repairs that can be done without expert knowledge and at low cost are part of the tenant's minor maintenance.
130394.m: The tenant pays for small repairs.

130395.q: Why is it worth keeping photos and receipts of valuable things in the flat?
a: So you can prove their value to the insurer after damage
So burglars know what there is
So you can show them on social media
130395.e: After a fire or a break-in the contents insurance wants to know what was lost and how much it was worth.

130396.q: In a block of flats, what is usually your duty after doing your washing?
a: Leave the laundry room and machine clean and on time
Dismantle the machine after each wash
130396.e: The house rules govern the laundry room. Leaving it on time and clean avoids disputes.
130396.m: Leave the laundry room as I would like to find it.

130397.q: You return a phone you found to its owner. Are you entitled to a reward?
a: Yes, to a reasonable finder's reward
Yes, to the full value of the phone
130397.e: Anyone who hands something in can ask the owner for a reasonable finder's reward. Anyone who keeps what they find, on the other hand, commits an offence.
130397.m: Handing in what you find pays off.

130398.q: What does a 15-year-old need to ride an e-scooter with a motor up to 20 km/h on the road?
a: A number plate from the municipality
130398.e: E-scooters count, like slow e-bikes, as light mopeds. Between 14 and 16 you need a category M licence.
130398.m: E-scooter from 14 to 16 only with an M licence.

130399.q: What applies to mobile phones when driving in Switzerland?
a: Phoning is only allowed with a hands-free system
Texting is always allowed at traffic lights
You may hold it in your hand while driving
130399.e: Anyone holding a phone at the wheel risks a fine. Texting is especially distracting.

130400.q: Malik has two apprenticeships on offer and accepts one. What does he do about the other?
a: Turn it down quickly and politely
Simply not turn up on the first day
130400.e: A quick refusal lets the company give the place to someone else. That is fair.
130400.m: Turning down offers is part of fair dealing.

130401.q: By when must notice of cancellation of a contract normally reach the recipient?
a: On the last day of the contract
Some time in the same year
130401.e: For contracts such as tenancies or subscriptions, what usually counts is when the notice arrives, not when it was sent. So you send it early enough.
130401.m: Send notices of cancellation in good time.

130402.q: Why is it best to be present yourself at the handover of your old flat?
a: So you can discuss and sign the damage in the handover report
Because otherwise the landlord cannot find the flat
Because you get the deposit in cash there
Because otherwise the service charges are doubled
130402.e: The handover report records which damage the landlord has found. If you are present, you can object and sign nothing you disagree with.
130402.m: Be present yourself at the flat handover.
